investmentDescription: PHIMT is comprised of dual applications. The primary application is a secure web-based application that enables all MHS entities to process, manage, track, route and maintain patient Protected Health Information (PHI)-related disclosures, authorizations, restrictions, complaints, confidential communications, authorized & unauthorized releases and other legal requirements related to compliance with the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) Privacy Act and the HITECH(ARRA) rule. PHIMT is the only Military Health System (MHS) enterprise-wide tool designed and used for these regulatory and compliance purposes and is available to the MHS user community under an enterprise license covering Military Treatment Facilities (MTFs), including dental facilities. PHIMT provides the MHS enterprise with a means of tracking, processing, routing and storing HIPAA compliance information about patient (PHI), disclosures, authorizations, releases, restrictions, requests, and complaints. PHIMT is also used for authorizing and tracking third-party PHI requests. PHIMT helps ensure that the MHS, as a covered entity, maintains a history of when and to whom disclosures of PHI are made.  PHIMT stores information about disclosures, authorizations, and restrictions that are made for a particular patient and can provide an accounting of disclosures via streamlined disclosure process. PHIMT provides an accounting of these disclosures to an individual upon request, and track authorizations and restrictions related to PHI made by the individual.  PHIMT automates the adoption of new MHS privacy policies, procedures, and regulations across the enterprise and provides a complete accounting of records upon request.  The other application, DHA-FOIA is utilized to process Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) and Privacy Act, appeal, Litigation, and Consultation requests. It electronically creates requests, stores requester details, and allows analysts to upload redacted documents for delivery to requester. It also has data and analytic capabilities to track FOIA processing statistics/fees and generates reports on the number/types/disposition of requests, as required by the Department of Justice (DOJ). PHIMT is currently in the Operations and Support lifecycle phase.

investmentDescription: PCOS includes TRICARE Encounter Data and Patient Encounter Processing and Reporting applications. TED is a data set of information for all purchased health care delivered under the TRICARE Contracts.  The TED patients encounter record processing addresses the government's need for timely access to health care information and fully encompasses the government goal for modernization and incorporation of Health Care Insurance Portability and Accountability Act requirements and standards.  The TED application verifies the Managed Care Support Contractors submitted record of encounter by applying business rules (also referred to as TED Edits), and provides results back to the MCSC.PEPR is a web-based suite of applications which enable analysis of purchased care patient encounter records generated by the MCSCs aligned to TRICARE contracts.  PEPR features standardized and ad hoc reporting capabilities designed for specific end user requirements.  Available data is used for fraud and abuse identification, duplicate claim data identification and provider and beneficiary research.  The information delivered by PEPR is used to track and report dollars used in annual government health care expenses, fraudulent activities, improper payments, duplicate claims activity, and to provide analysis of health care cost and utilization.  This initiative is a split investment from the original Executive Information/Decision Support initiative for reporting purposes. The subset of care provided under TRICARE by non-military physicians, hospitals, pharmacies, and suppliers is referred to as purchased care. PCOS is the only system that processes the TRICARE purchased care claims, stores the associated data, and provides tailored data and reports on these claims.  PCOS data and reports are used by all levels of the MHS organization to: detect fraud, waste, and abuse; identify and recoup duplicate claims payments; respond to congressional inquiries; perform claims review audits and monitor contractor performance; develop trends and budget projections; respond to requests from Senior DHA leadership; provide information to DOJ; and inform service branch representatives with information on care being delivered to enrolled beneficiaries.  PCOS reports visualize billions of dollars in annual government healthcare expenses. PCOS reports enable the prompt payment of civilian healthcare provider claims within 24 hours which is necessary to support payment process to providers within 30 days.

investmentDescription: The WebEOC system provides coordinated emergency management operations to help prepare for, mitigate, respond to and recover from natural or man-made disasters. Airmen and family members are at risk without the ability to communicate emergency needs across AETC as well as installation.  Proper allocation and deployment of critical emergency management assets will be seriously hindered; potentially causing more damage, injury or deaths in the event of crisis. WebEOC provides AETC Installation's leadership access to real-time information for a common operating picture during emergency and daily operations.  Further, it serves as a critically needed communication tool that will enable collaboration with decision makers at federal, state and local agencies, healthcare providers and other community resources.  Current methods of communication e.g., telephone, fax, and email are a secondary means for communication and coordination which become quickly overwhelmed during emergencies. WebEOC is the standard communication means for the Office of Homeland Security and its subordinate organizations; Emergency Operation Centers across the nation are currently migrating towards this system to create a seamless network of emergency response throughout the Country. WebEOC is a Crisis Information Management System and is designed to operate on Windows Server 2003 or 2008.  The system consists of web servers and database servers. WebEOC is designed to operate with the state and local surrounding areas.  WebEOC has been designed to operate on a PDA running Microsoft Windows Mobile version 5 or 6. Blackberry? support is provided via the Blackberry OS browser, version 4.2.1 on the Cingular and AT&T networks. Opera is also supported on the Blackberry via any network. WebEOC can also run in a virtual environment.  WebEOC was accredited at Fort Bragg as part of the I2MC (Integrated Incident Management Center) system listed in Army Portfolio Management as DA176395.  The I2MC includes a 911 Emergency Response center that operates 24 hours a day, 7 days a week as do AETC Installations.  WebEOC handles information that is determined to be vital to the operational readiness or mission effectiveness of deployed and contingency forces in terms of both content and timeliness. The consequences of loss of integrity or availability of WebEOC would be unacceptable and could include the immediate and sustained loss of mission effectiveness.

investmentDescription: The Human Resources Information Systems (HRIS) provide organizations, DFAS Senior Management, DFAS employees and the HR community with access to the business intelligence needed to make strategic human capital decisions. HRIS is comprised of Human Resources Business Intelligence Datamart (HRBID), Request for Personnel Actions (RPA), Electronic Data Interchange Person Identifier (EDIPI), Personnel Accountability Tracker (PAT), Employee Voluntary Early Retirement Authority/Voluntary Separation Incentive Pay (eVERA/VSIP), and the Learning Management System (LMS). HRBID personally identifiable information (PII) data collected is used strictly for data matching while allowing users who have a validated need to know ability to run standard reports and ad hoc queries against the HRBID data via HRBID Cognos.  PII data consists of SSN, citizenship, mailing/home address, home phone number, demographics, employment information, education information, gender, personnel email address, military records, and race/ethnicity. The LMS module allows authorized users the capability to manage their learning and development activities.    The RPA module gathers PII information (employee name, employment information) to track and report the progress of personnel actions. EDIPI is used by applications throughout DFAS to uniquely and unambiguously identify DoD personnel, including agency information. PII information collected by EDIPI is person's name, social security number, service, rank, pay plan, work email, date of birth, and government agency code. PAT is an automated tool for use in support of DODI 3001.02 Personnel Accountability events (Specifically, accounting for our employees following a natural or man-made disaster).  The tool will take input from the DMDC's PARS tool (file upload to PAT, not a direct connection), merge with existing DCPDS data, allow statusing of employees (present, on leave, injured, deceased, etc.) and output personnel statuses in the prescribed PARS file format.  eVERA/VSIP VERA/VSIP is used to avoid or minimize the need for involuntary separations and demotions when activities are undergoing reduction in force, reorganization, base closure, reduction in work, or transfer of function outside of the commuting area. VERA/VSIP may also be used to restructure the workforce to meet mission objectives without reducing the overall number of personnel.

investmentTitle: Global Theater Security Cooperation Management Information Systems (G-TSCMIS)
investmentDescription: Global Theater Security Cooperation Management information Systems (G-TSCMIS) Program is an Office of the Secretary of Defense (OSD) initiative to develop and deploy a common web-based, centrally hosted Management Information System (MIS) that will serve as the information focus point for the Nation?s Security Cooperation (SC) efforts by providing decision makers, SC planners and other users with the ability to view, manage, assess, and report SC activities and events.  G-TSCMIS will consolidate, improve upon and is intended to replace all existing TSCMIS solutions hosted at and supporting more than 20 Department of Defense (DoD) Services, Agencies and Combatant Commands (CCDRs).  It will provide a comprehensive picture of whole-of-government SC activities, and will contribute to planning more effective cooperative security activities to align or meet desired outcomes in support of SC end states.    G-TSCMIS is a fully interoperable component of Adaptive Planning and Execution (APEX) and the DoD Joint C2 (JC2) Capability.  The effort will support the strategic planning of CCDRs by providing access to reports of programs, activities, events, funding, assessments, and status of achieving defined end states.  G-TSCMIS will provide visualization, assessment, reporting, and data management throughout the conduct of SC activities planning and execution phases. Information from the SC activities will be binned by separate SC programs, budget lines/funding streams, equipment drawdown, etc.  This will enable users at the tactical level to focus on specific programs, participating forces, events, and activities, while users at the strategic level will be able to access summary reports of geographic regions, resource requirements, or total expenditure of funds by source.   G-TSCMIS interfaces with other systems, such as Joint Training Information Management System (JTIMS), Joint Capability Requirements Manager (JCRM) and Defense Readiness Reporting System (DRRS).  G-TSCMIS must also be interoperable with the other United States Government (USG) foreign assistance and international cooperation information systems.  G-TSCMIS will allow decision makers and analysts to identify redundant investments, plan more effective engagements, and find gaps and opportunities for building more capable partners.

investmentDescription: The SBCR App was mandated by the ASN(RDA) memorandum entitled ?Small Business Coordination Review Application? dated 2 Feb 2016 for all of DON to utilize the system to automate the generation of the Small Business Coordination Record (DD 2579). The mandate was also incorporated into the Navy Marine Corps Acquisition Regulation Supplement (NMCARS) per Change 13-10, 5219.201 (c)(10)(B), September 2013 edition. As required in DFARS 219.201, the Contracting activity small business (SB) specialist must review and make recommendations for all acquisitions over $10K, except those under the simplified acquisition threshold that are totally set aside for SB concerns in accordance with the FAR. This review must take place before issuance of a solicitation or contract action and be documented on the DD Form 2579, SB Coordination Record, which is a paper form. The SBCR App automated the review process which includes the contracting officer who is responsible for the coordination and completion of the form, the contracting activity small business specialist and Small Business Administration Procurement Center Representative that reviews and concurs or non-concurs with the action. There have been over 130,000 contract actions generated in the SBCR App across the DON and currently over 4,800 active users. Immediate benefits of the tool include coordination time savings, improved data quality and availability of raw data to develop more accurate procurement forecasts. Long term benefits include centralized collection of data allows derivative analysis and forecasting, automated market research to provide information for informed decision making (i.e. Rule of 2) and workload reporting. Additionally, the new ePS (Electronic Procurement System) Requirements Specification lists states that ?The system shall provide a web link to the SBCR homepage from within the application? along with other specifications (SMI-09.02, DBB-66, DBB-67, DBB-68, PLP-01, PLP-02, and PLP-030) shall conform to the SBCR App that was awarded. If the SBCR App is not funded, the workforce will revert to using the manual process for coordination of the DD Form 2579 potentially adding time to the schedule and impacting data quality. The funding keeps the DD 2579 process efficient by being automated and current with policies and procedures.

investmentDescription: Air Combat Command (ACC) has determined the need to train aircraft, especially fifth generation aircraft aircrews against modern surface-to-air missile (SAM) threats. To satisfy this training requirement, the Advanced Radar Threat System (ARTS) Program requires the development of multiple modern system variants. These variants include short range, medium range, and long range SAM threats Within these range requirements, mobile (track and shoot on the move), tactical, and strategic level threats are supported. The ARTS Program Office is planning on purchasing sufficient quantities of each system to support the threat densities at the Combat Air Force (CAF) training ranges needed for aircrew training in multiple scenarios. The ARTS Program Office is tasked to manage the entire development cycle. investmentDescription: S-IRIS offers evidence-based aviation mishap prevention through regular analysis of digital flight data, providing a baseline for day-to-day operations and identifying deviations from standards. The resulting qualitative and quantitative information enhances warfighter hazard awareness and system effectiveness. S-IRIS addresses the human factors of flying operations ? what extraneous events cause pilots to fly the aircraft counter to guidance or accepted standards, and how to mitigate those influences. Mitigation measures focus on risk reduction and performance behaviors to maximize individual and collective warfighter performance. Benefits include mishap reduction, resource conservation, risk awareness, and data-driven decision-making. Architectural dependencies include the Aircraft Structural Integrity Management Information System and G081. These IT systems provide flight data files for processing through software unique to each fleet. Per DoD requirement the AF initiates flight data analysis on one additional fleet each year. As of 2018, the web-based S-IRIS system includes 12 aircraft fleets (17 variants), providing risk exposure information to flying organizations across the AF, sister services, and several foreign partners. S-IRIS captures routine measurements (snapshots of data at particular points in each flight) and triggered events (exceedances) in an analysis results file. Query tools produce trend reports and hazard identification products. Customized analyses depict operations and hazards at specific locations, for specific aircraft, at specific times of year. S-IRIS aircraft analysts review the results and prepare monthly status reports for units, MAJCOMs, sister services, and foreign partners. Reports include trending of known hazards, analysis of newly identified hazards, and customer-specific interest areas. Leadership utilizes the results to modify flight operations (training, maneuvers and procedures, current requirements) and/or guidance (policy, flight manuals) to mitigate or remove hazard causal factors. Beneficiaries range from pilots and flight crews in their day-to-day operations, through senior leaders in their role as risk managers. Commanders employ risk management to either accept the risk as needed for mission accomplishment or mitigate the cause. The Air Force Safety Center manages S-IRIS activity through a software and analysis manpower contract. No earlier incarnation of this investment exists.

investmentDescription: The Guaranteeing AI Robustness against Deception (GARD) program, expanding on technical challenges encountered in the Lifelong Learning Machines program, will develop techniques to make artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) algorithms and systems more robust in the presence of deceptive data and adversarial attack. Concurrent with the recent explosion of interest in ML, deception attacks that manipulate a ML system into an  erroneous response have also emerged. While such deception attacks against ML have become sophisticated and varied, the development of  defensive capabilities for ML systems has not been maintained. The GARD program will address the growing need for defensive ML capabilities by developing techniques to establish robustness properties of ML systems, and to defend against possible attacks. The techniques developed under GARD will be essential if the DoD is to rely on ML systems in contested environments.

investmentDescription: The web based Total Employee Development (TED) system is a paperless training tool used by Army Material Command (AMC) Headquarters as an Enterprise Training Tracking System. TED is also used by over 20 Non-AMC organizations.  AMC has directed training management in TED for both Logistics Modernization Program (LMP) and mandatory training. The TED system supports over 65,000 people and is used to request, schedule, approve, monitor and report on both mandatory and career broadening training requirements for each individual within the organizations.  TED can also be used to track training funds by individual and/or organization but does not allocate funds.  TED is accessed by all individuals in the commands through the employee, supervisor, instructor, coordinator, administrator, or the financial coordinator module to request and track training.  The TED system automatically informs supervisors and any necessary personnel by email of information relevant to their training and generates training requests for supervisor approval.  TED interfaces with Career Acquisition Personnel & Position Management Information System (CAPPMIS) to update Individual Development Plan (IDP) information on a real-time basis.  TED tracks training hours and provides employees and supervisors with an IDP feature to ensure a fully trained and well-rounded work force.  TED issues a number of types of reports to include  a detailed financial (for tracking purposes only, and ad hoc reports as well as auto populating the Standard Form 182 if funds are required. The capabilities TED provides to AMC, its Major Subordinate Commands and additional users are vital to ensure training requirements are met.  Without these capabilities, over 65K employees would be required to process and track training requirements manually or develop new computer or paper files to fulfill the same functions.

investmentDescription: VCE enables total visibility and analysis of all elements of the contracting mission. The warehouse is a database that products connect to in order to pull required data.  This product supports planning and analysis of multiple business areas to including Acquisition, Finance, Inventory Warehousing, Requisitions/Sales Orders, Provisioning, Logistics,  Material Master and Supply Chain Planning.  Logistics Modernization Program (LMP) developers created data extracts that populate the Logistics Support Activity (LOGSA) warehouse. The AMCOM RDAW receives its data from LOGSA. The data warehouse is not only used locally but across other commands to support decision making tools and analysis.  Multiple applications located in multiple organizations/locations pull the data to be used in products.  The AMCOM RDAW is hosted by Aviation and Missile Command (AMCOM) G6 and located at Redstone Arsenal. RDAW is Enterprise and will transition to a future Cloud environment once it is modernized.

It was developed in response to and in support of Army Regulation 25-30.  AMCOM IADS renders interactive displays of various aspects of technical data such as maintenance procedures, repair part and special tool lists, technical drawings and illustrations, maintenance work requirements, instructional videos, product support data, and critical flight and usage safety information.  AMCOM IADS also provides usability and efficiency improvements over conventional documentation by providing document navigation via an interactive table of contents, hyperlinks, history, indexing and search capabilities.  AMCOM IADS is freely distributed and updated from a static/non-application website.  AMCOM IADS customer base includes the Warfighter, Department of Defense (DOD) civilian and contractors, as well as private sector vendors and users worldwide.

AMCOM IADS is an application that provides IETM/ETM functionality for weapon system tech data and publications.  AMCOM IADS was designed to require minimum effort to produce an IETM from source files such as Standard Generalized Markup Language (SGML)/Extensible Markup Language (XML)/Hypertext Markup Language (HTML).  Navigation is provided via the table of contents, hyperlinks/hotspots, history, indexing and search.  Users can add bookmarks, notes (including attachments), and critical safety messages such as Safety of Flight (SOF) notifications.  AMCOM IADS supports multiple multimedia formats including vector and raster images, videos, and Adobe Flash.  AMCOM IADS 4.0 provides a more robust printing capability (with embedded graphics) than in previous versions.

investmentDescription: Department of the Navy's Limited Duty Program is a Service Headquarters Program in which Navy Medicine has a key role. Limited Duty (LIMDU) is a period of "medically restricted" duty due to an illness, injury, or disease. The LIMDU program is currently tracked in a system called Medical Board Online Tracking System (MEDBOLTS) which outlived its usefulness. LIMDU SMART allows Navy Medicine to respond to increasing requirements of a complex patient population. The Naval Audit Service conducted a review of the Navy Limited Duty (LIMDU) program in 2012. Findings determined additional personnel, critical to managing the LIMDU program, needed access to data to more effectively manage the wounded service members on limited duty. MEDBOLTS didn?t provide an effective population management tool or viable metrics. Service members were spending more days on limited duty than needed and thus not able to perform their assigned duties. Fleet readiness is impacted and manpower lost due to labor intensive processes that impact the LIMDU Program and cause delays in processing LIMDU cases. MEDBOLTS software needed to be upgraded to a more secure, easier to maintain architecture to support new requirements and comply with the audit findings. LIMDU SMART provides Navy and Marine Corps with real-time visibility of all personnel on limited duty, run reports on all aspects of LIMDU Program, electronically manage workflows, and securely send medical documents associated with the service person?s treatment. LIMDU SMART provides enhanced visibility of personnel by automating and standardizing key elements of the workflow processes. Full visibility of all Sailors and Marines assigned to Limited Duty will support overall readiness status. Through workflow automation and process improvement, users can compile key data elements by utilizing LIMDU SMART?s Business Intelligence software from which analytical reports and dashboards depicting readiness and care management can be instantly generated. LIMDU SMART?s data ?at-a-glance? feature effectively provides visibility of all Sailors? and Marines? limited duty status while safeguarding service member?s Personal Identification Information (PII) through role-based access and read/write audit trails. Developed with built-in system scalability, LIMDU SMART modernizes the current paper-based LIMDU program, providing force strength clarity and comprehensive insight into service member?s care via a centralized, web-based application.

The Civilian Manpower Module implements Department of the Navy (DoN) comptroller standardized Civilian Manpower pricing techniques at each accounting level (i.e., Appropriation, Budget Activity, Activity Group, and Sub-Activity Group) within NAVAIR. The module is responsible for consolidating NAVAIR field activity budgets into an automated claimant submission as required by DoN comptroller. The module also provides and maintains official NAVAIR Civilian Manpower budget data (CP-2 and CP-3 Exhibits) in archival format. OP-32 Report Building Module. The module is responsible for consolidating NAVAIR O&M,N programs into an automated claimant submission as required by DoN comptroller. The module also maintains official NAVAIR O&M,N as well as Operations & Maintenance, Navy Reserve (O&MN,NR) budget data (NC-1, PB-15, PB-18, PB-18a, OP-26, and OP-32 Exhibits) in electronic format. Funding Controls Module. The Funding Controls module maintains accurate records of DoN budget controls, revised at each budget submission, in electronic format for current and archival use. The module tracks changes in budget controls by budget issue and by program. It is used as the primary means of distributing budget controls to program managers.

investmentDescription: The BUILDER Sustainment Management System (SMS) is suite of web-based software applications designed to help facility engineers, technicians, and managers decide when, where, and how to best maintain the built environment. The SMS modules include BUILDER and ROOFER for assessing building conditions, PAVER for pavements, and RAILER for railroad infrastructure.  New modules being developed are Utilities SMS for utilities assets, and FUELER for fuel systems. Current requirements include data interface with the Installation Status Report (ISR) system to properly transfer data with additional Army systems. Additionally, ongoing work will be required to consolidate modules and modernize the Enterprise SMS software/suite. SMS provides the Army, the OSD required standardized process, for calculation of the Facility Condition Index (FCI), facility condition inventory, assessments, work requirements analysis, and forecasting.   On 10 September 2013, the Under Secretary of Defense directed all the Services to adopt the Sustainment Management System (SMS) Suite consisting of the BUILDER, PAVER, and RAILER and other modules being developed to assess the condition of their real property facilities and to compute the Facility Condition Index (FCI).  Congress expressed concerns that the Services were not conducting facility condition assessments in a consistent manner, leading to inaccurate funding decisions.  The FCIs generated across the Services were not using the same evaluation tools and computational methods.  In the 2012 NDAA, Congress directed DoD to correct this problem.  To resolve this issue, the Army must integrate the FCI data generated in the SMS evaluations, with information in the Headquarters Installation Information System (HQIIS) and Installation Status Report (ISRWEB).

It relies on a Windows Server 2003 Operating System (OS) to execute.  The OS will be provided and maintained by NEC-R and is not dedicated to MEARS.  MEARS will not have interfaces with any other application or system.  The data that is utilized by MEARS will be housed on a NEC-R Managed SQL Server 2005 database server using a Windows 2003 Operating System that resides within the Redstone ICAN accreditation boundary.

Each year, CMMI launches models that require technology solutions.  These models have diverse needs, and managing operations requires a great deal of coordination across the CMMI and CMS.  The investment supports the following IT Strategy to meet these business needs.

investmentDescription: The Reserve End Item Management System (REIMS) is a web-based software application developed for the United States Army Reserve (USAR) to assist with the management of Class II, Class IV, and Class VII property book items at multiple levels of visibility.  It provides an automated ability to track the quantity and dollar value of excess, the method to track and make lateral transfers with supporting documentation, turn-ins,  notifies units of disposition action, and provides the only means for the USAR to track equipment in depot maintenance.  Provides asset managers with a one-stop system that furnishes asset visibility and equipment redistribution capabilities while assisting units at all levels in making accurate and timely equipment redistribution decisions.  It provides the ability to query the supply and shipment status posted in the Property Book Unit Supply-Enhanced (PBUSE) master files. Users may access the system through the Internet using a Web Browser and query multiple database elements in any of the modules.  Input to this system is from PBUSE.  Excesses and shortages are easily determined with 100 percent accuracy.  Once a manager makes a lateral transfer or turn-in decision, the gaining/losing units are automatically notified through electronic media.  Users of the system are the item managers at the US Army Reserve Command, Regional Readiness Command and Direct Reporting Command levels as well as property book and unit supply personnel. partOfITPortfolio: Part 2. IT Investments for Mission Support Services
investmentDescription: The Key Control Automated Key Management System maintains positive control over keys to high-security locks securing US Army ammunition storage buildings. The system integrates several technologies to automatically identify users (key custodians and key recipients), read key numbers, and record transaction details. It also enforces certain security criteria to ensure that only properly authorized individuals are able to draw the keys to any particular building. In summary, Key Control automates all verification and data collection activities associated with each key issue and receipt transaction. The Key Control system includes hardware devices integrated with a custom software application. Key room personnel can login using a password or by Common Access Card (CAC). The system identifies precisely which key(s) an individual is checking in or out by reading a passive Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) device attached to each key. It then reads data from the recipient?s government-issued Common Access Card (CAC) to record the user?s identity, and collects a digital signature from the recipient to establish proof that the transaction occurred. Using relationships and restrictions stored in its database, Key Control identifies the building to which each scanned key belongs, and checks to ensure that the recipient only receives keys to buildings for which he or she has authorized access. Several categories of authorization are supported, including security classification, storage category, owning activity, and special access limitations. All relevant conditions must be met before the system will process the transaction. Key Control includes a number of standard reports designed to support various user requirements:   ?	All keys currently outstanding ?	All keys issued to a particular user ?	All buildings in which material has been moved for a particular date ?	All key issue transactions for a given date ?	All key issue/receipt transactions for a specified building over a specified time period ?	All key inventory stored in the Key Control database ?	Key control user security clearance status ?	Digital signatures verification report.

investmentTitle: IMCOM WILDLIFE AND LAND MANAGEMENT SYSTEM
investmentDescription: iSportsman is an interactive system developed to address the overwhelming and ever-growing issues in managing recreational activities across military, government, and private lands.  Natural resource managers are often challenged to effectively handle the onslaught of growing public demand to use its lands in a fair and safe manner.  Military installations add another layer of complexity for land managers due to the main mission of training soldiers with live fire and other field operations that coexist with ancillary public recreation opportunities.  iSportsman aims to help resource managers to properly manage all recreational activities, including hunting, fishing, hiking, biking, boating, and camping, within their respective lands and to collect necessary harvest information from users and track usage to facilitate effective and sustainable multipurpose use of resources.  iSportsman is a service, not software, so it does not require anything to be installed on any government computers (or devices).  It also is not hosted on the .mil domain. For this reason, there is no need for local installation or base IT personnel involvement.  A key requirement of Department of Defense facilities is to ensure compliance with the Sikes Act, a part of which is to provide access to uniformed personnel, family members and the public to hunting, fishing and trapping.  This service allow for permit sales, permit lotteries, transaction reporting using pay.gov accounts, check in/out for hunting and fishing programs, harvest reporting, public safety education training, features a find me or panic feature to alert program administrators and/or security in the event of an emergency, allows better checks and controls for the Conservation Law Enforcement Officers, range control scheduling of areas open/closed due to military training operations, and allows for access control/security.  All performed online through a web service or using electronic kiosks.  No direct funded personnel costs are required to have a full time person sitting and waiting to sell permits or check in/out hunters/fishers.  Significant pay funding savings can be garnered by implementing this service.  It will also standardize how the Army manages outdoor recreation programs across every Army installation.  A Solider or his family members know the system and how it operates no matter what installation they are on if they plan on using the outdoor recreation programs the installation has to offer.

investmentDescription: The Joint Analytic Real-time Virtual Information Sharing System (JARVISS) provides the Army, Navy and other DOD partners with the capability to facilitate real-time sharing of threat information as events/incidents unfold. The system will allow the real-time sharing of threat information with a variety of users at DOD installations, Stand-Alone Facilities (SAFs), commands and units to appropriately increase their security posture and appropriately respond to threats to protect personnel and assets.   The system is currently in use by all Army commands and is being fielded to installations across the Army.  Additional DOD users currently include the Navy. The system shares real-time threat information as required by DOD 5200.12 and Army Regulations 525-13 and 190-45.  The system will geo-locate and display all critical data (e.g., type, time/date, and location) of specific event/incidents (e.g., active shooter, suspicious activity, bomb threats, chemical incident, explosion, hazardous incident, power outage, radiological incident, or transportation incident).  JARVISS has the capability for organizations to configure their own business rules for threat information that is most important or relevant to their mission.  JARVISS is designed to feed-in and extract threat data from current and future Government and commercial data bases.  It can ingest information from various current and future social media sources as well as various open-source, government data layers.  JARVISS facilitates the real-time sharing of threat information using a cloud-based web application from a desktop or laptop computer or through the use of a mobile application on handheld devices such as smart phones and tablets.

The I3MP infrastructure provides tactical and strategic end-users with connectivity from the desktop to the DOD Information Networks (DODIN) and is at the very foundation of the Army's Enterprise IT modernization strategy, Network 2025, to evolve to an Everything over Internet Protocol (EoIP) network environment that meets the DoD mandate to implement Unified Capabilities (UC) and the Joint Information Environment (JIE).   The installation-level network infrastructure is comprised of the wiring, electronics, and security equipment required to provide voice, video, and data communications to traditional business users and Warfighters alike.  Specific systems include classified and unclassified Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP), Joint Regional Security Stacks, and Internet Protocol Video.  

The I3MP network modernization implementation plan engineers, designs, and fields the standardized, converged, UC-ready, secure Installation Campus Area Network (ICAN) infrastructure using Commercial-off-the-Shelf (COTS) solutions.  It will enable Soldiers to maintain their warfighting systems, and proficiency on those systems, from their home station rather than relying on costly satellite usage time.  I3MP modernization also supports training and readiness as it provides the critical high speed and high bandwidth connectivity required for facilities and organizations to conduct Live, Virtual, and Constructive exercises and operations. 

In Korea, I3MP continues to support IT engineering for the Yongsan Relocation Plan/Land Partnership Plan to reduce the U.S. forces footprint and consolidate operations at Camp Humphries.  It also resources the communications network backbone infrastructure supporting Joint communications on the peninsula with phased replacement of the obsolete Asynchronous Transfer Mode (ATM) /Synchronous Optical Networking (SONET) infrastructure that consists of 62 ATM nodes (circa 1997) and 28 SONET nodes (circa 1999), that provide data, voice, and video between 55 US military installations.

investmentDescription:
The Integrated Logistics Support Center (ILSC) Supply, Maintenance and Cost Analysis Tool (SMCAT) is a Web-based tool designed to provide senior leadership and the Tank-Automotive and Armaments Command (TACOM), currently known as TACOM Life Cycle Management Command, community with logistics execution figures and information to assess the readiness posture, overall health and supportability of the weapon systems managed by the ILSC. The application currently manages approximately 70 execution indicators in 20 different logistic subject areas for major and secondary items.  Data is regularly extracted at a very granular level from a wide variety of sources covering a range of logistic domains, and is then retained for extended periods.  The application is thus able to publish statistics and reports not available from any other source and provide extensive historical trend analysis.   The combination of data from multiple domains allows the ILSC to add significant extra dimensions to basic analysis.   For example, the combination of Defense Logistics Agency storage data with logistics data from Logistics Modernization Program (LMP) and Major Item data from Logistics Support Activity (LOGSA) has provided key insights into overhead expenditure and allowed the ILSC to both transfer storage charges to Program Executive Offices (PEOs) and to target other specific actions to achieve overhead cost reduction.  

The tool is also widely used in the Sales and Operations Planning (S&OP) exercises.  Reports have been created that allow for the analysis and tracing of changes or ?spikes? in a target month and the comparison between successive months data to identify individual items causing any anomalies.  Additionally, the S&OP Demand summary reports have been extended below the sub-family level to Weapon System and individual item views.   These advanced analytic capabilities have saved all of the directorates significant amounts of time and greatly improved the accuracy of the submissions to Army Materiel Command.

investmentDescription: The ARMoR-D will be used by the Multidrug-resistant Organism Repository and Surveillance Network ("MRSN") in its response to the epidemic of multidrug-resistant infections in traumatically injured Wounded Warriors; and the increased risk infections by multidrug resistant organism (MDROs) presents to the Military Health System (MHS). To date there has been no enterprise effort to collect or characterize these bacterial isolates in order to inform best practice, such as patient management and antibiotic selection. ARMOR-D will support performance improvement, infection control, and the complicated management of battlefield injury related infections. ARMOR-D will provide an immediate impact to deployed and fixed facilities in the MHS. It will include requirements derived from the full spectrum of Army Medical Command (MEDCOM) stakeholders, including health care providers, consultants to the Surgeon General, infection preventionists, and information management personnel. ARMOR-D collects and manages the data from Military Treatment Facilities (MTF`s) and the MRSN`s centralized laboratory, and helps the MRSN unburden enrolled MTF clinical laboratories of outbreak investigation, and inform clinicians and medical policy leaders. ARMOR-D will be comprised of a central database at the Walter Reed Army Institute of Research (WRAIR) that catalogues bacterial isolates and drug sensitivity data relevant to instances of MDROs. Isolates received (from MTFs or other sources) are labeled and recorded in the ARMOR-D for future retrieval. Sensitivity data provided with the isolates is imported into the ARMOR-D. Data from additional tests performed by ARMOR-D program staff, including genetic sequence related data are also imported into the ARMOR-D. The system will be accessed via a web browser interface, by authenticated users, across the intranet/internet. This will grant the healthcare and research communities access to composite antibiograms and isolate information for analysis and correlation, and for investigation of future outbreaks of known or unknown MDROs. This initiative was previously known as Multidrug-resistant Organism Repository and Surveillance Network (MRSN) "application".  This was too similar to the organization's name and caused confusion.  The name was changed to better separate references to the IT system from references to the organization.

investmentDescription: Basic research. This program seeks to develop innovative mathematical methods and fast, reliable and scalable algorithms aimed at making radical advances in computational science and large-scale engineering and design. Research in computational mathematics underpins the fundamental understanding of complex physical phenomena and leads to predictive simulation capabilities that are crucial to the design and control of future U.S. Air Force systems, and their lifetime expectancy. Proposals to this program should focus on fundamental scientific and mathematical innovations, and should have the potential to address some of the most important computational challenges in science and engineering. Additionally, it is desirable to frame the basic research ideas in the context of applications relevant to the U.S. Air Force, which can serve simultaneously to focus the research and to provide avenues for transition of basic research outcomes into practice. Applications of current Air Force interest include, but are not limited to, quantum physics and quantum information systems, plasma dynamics, turbulence (e.g., in fluids, combustion, plasma), lasers and directed energy, aero-thermo-dynamics, information science, data analysis (including machine learning), biophysics, and material and structural sciences.

partOfITPortfolio: Part 3. IT Standard IT Investments
investmentDescription: Basic research. This program emphasizes the interplay of dynamical systems and control theories with the future aim of developing innovative synergistic strategies for the design and analysis of controlled systems that enable radically enhanced capabilities, including performance and operational efficiency for future U.S. Air Force systems. Proposals should focus on the fundamental science and mathematics first, but should also include possible connectivity to appropriate Air Force applications of the future. These applications currently include information systems, as well as autonomous/semi-autonomous aerial vehicles, munitions, and space vehicles. The dramatic increase in complexity of Air Force systems provides unique challenges for the Dynamics and Control Program. Meeting these challenges may require interdisciplinary approaches as well as deeper studies within single disciplines.? Lastly, note that the Dynamics and Control Program places special emphasis on mathematically rigorous techniques addressing realistic treatment of applications, complexity management, semi-autonomous systems, and real-time operation in stochastic and adversarial environments.

investmentDescription: Basic research. This program supports innovative basic research on the fundamental principles and methodologies needed to enable intelligent machine behavior, particularly in support of mixed-initiative (i.e., human-machine teaming) systems. The overall vision of this program is that future computational systems will achieve high levels of performance, adaptation, flexibility, self-repair, and other forms of intelligent behavior in the complex, uncertain, adversarial, and highly dynamic environments faced by the U.S. Air Force. This program covers the full spectrum of computational and machine intelligence, from cognitively plausible reasoning processes that are responsible for human performance in complex problem-solving and decision-making tasks, to non-cognitive computational models of intelligence necessary to create robust intelligent systems. Robustness in this context is the ability to achieve high performance given at least some or all of the following factors: uncertainty, incompleteness or errors in knowledge; limitations on sensing; real-world complexity and dynamic change; adversarial factors; unexpected events including system faults; and out-of-scope requirements on system behavior. In the midst of this spectrum are the technologies explicitly needed to seamlessly incorporate intelligent computational systems into mixed human-machine teams. The program is divided into three sub-areas that span the full spectrum of computational and machine intelligence. They are: Computational Cognition, Human-Machine Teaming and Machine Intelligence.  The program encourages cross-disciplinary teams with collaboration including computer scientists, neuroscientists, cognitive scientists, mathematicians, statisticians, operation and management science researchers, information scientists, econometricians and game theoreticians, etc., especially when the research pertains to common issues and when collaboration is likely to generate bidirectional benefits.

investmentDescription: Basic research.  Trust and Influence is an interdisciplinary basic research portfolio with two overarching goals. The first, is to advance our basic understanding of human reliance and teaming, to elucidate how people establish, maintain, and repair trust in agents, both human and machine. In particular, it supports research to build the scientific foundations for designing high-performing, mixed humans-machine teams, through properly calibrated trust. Research on the human social and cognitive process that inform the design of systems composed of human and machine agents and the development of novel man-machine interfaces and interaction techniques is of particular interest. The second goal is to advance the science of social influence within the context of national security. For instance, researchers in the program strive to understand the variables that influence human behavior, attitudes and beliefs, sufficient for measurement and forecasting of social phenomena. There is particular interest in developing computational approaches and using large-scale data sets to understand social and cultural behavior. Trust and Influence invests in the discovery of foundational concepts of effective influence, deterrence, trust-building, trust calibration, and counter-terrorism operations. Multidisciplinary and transdisciplinary approaches are encouraged, to include contributions from cognitive science, neuroscience, anthropology, sociology, linguistics, economics, computer science and mathematics. Research designs that incorporate laboratory studies, modeling or field research leading to transformative novel theories are encouraged.  See p. 28 of AFOSR BAA FA9550-18-S-0003 for details.

investmentTitle: Science of Information, Computation, Learning, and Fusion
investmentDescription: Basic research. The U.S. Air Force collects vast amounts of data through various modes at various times in order to extract and derive needed ?information? from these large and heterogeneous (mixed types) data sets. Some data, such as those collected from magnetometers, register limited information content which is more identifiable at the sensor level but beyond human?s sensory reception. Other types of data, such as video cameras or text reports, possess more semantic information that is closer to human cognition and understanding. Nevertheless, these are instances of disparate data which encapsulate different types of ?information? pertained to, perhaps, the same event(s) captured by different modalities through sensing and collection.  In order to understand and interpret information contained in various data sources, it is necessary to extract relevant pieces of information from these datasets and to make inferences based on prior knowledge and probabilities. This bottom-up processing direction needs conceptually driven reasoning to integrate or fuse the previously extracted snippets of information by leveraging domain knowledge. Furthermore, the top-down processes can offer causal explanation or causal inference, generate new hypotheses, verify or test hypotheses in light of observed datasets. Between the data-driven and conceptually-driven ends, there may reside different levels of abstraction in which information is partially extracted and aggregated based on the nature of applications.  See p. 27 of AFOSR BAA FA9550-18-S-0003 for details.

investmentDescription: AVCOM is a commercially developed service so it is purchased as a service annually. Contractor is tasked to take Illustrated Parts Breakdown (IPB) technical orders and other forms of technical data and build Bill of Materials (BOMs). The BOMs are linked across all other weapon systems data that is loaded into the AVCOM tool. The Air Force has been contracting for the AVCOM service since the late 1990s. It is a tool used by engineers, logistics specialists and contractors on contract to perform in-depth DMSMS analysis (usually at the Air Logistics Centers) to proactively manage parts obsolescence.  The obsolescence issue is that a manufacturer will decide to no longer build a part (due to changes in technology, markets, etc.).  However, the Air Force may still need the part for future repairs so it must look for other options (e.g. buy enough parts to last the remaining life of the system, find another manufacturer of the same part, design a new part, etc.).  AVCOM explores those options.  Currently there are more than 50 Air Force systems in the database.  New systems are continually being added but should be completed within five years.  For parts in the database, specialists do market analysis surveys to determine how likely a part will become obsolete.  Specialists log into the tool from their individual computers to perform analyses.  The results of the analyses are summarized in the database and displayed in a format that helps the Air Force proactively manage the ever increasing obsolescence issues.  The analyses have also corrected erroneous information in the Air Force Technical Orders and D200A API.

investmentDescription: Form 202s (Nonconforming Technical Assistance Request and Reply) are used by maintenance personnel at WR-ALC to report and seek engineering dispositions for problems found with C5, C17, C130, and F15 airframes and flight control and support systems. Forms 202s require coordination from various technical personnel including structure, system, safety, and environmental engineers, equipment specialists, TO managers, planners, and production supervisors. Maintenance personnel initiate form 202s and perform the repairs in accordance with the engineering instructions provided with the forms. The AFMC Form 202 Automated System allows the maintenance activities to initiate form 202s, and automatically route them to the engineering organizations. The system allows users and management to track form 202s to see how many 202s are being worked, how many 202s are closed, how many work-stoppage 202s are open, who is working the 202s, where the 202s have been sent and worked, how many 202s are delinquent, and much more. The system also enforces the users to follow the AFMC Manual 21-1 Chapter 5 policy guiding the Form 202 process. The system insures that all required signatures have been obtained and that all fields are completed correctly. By following the AFMCMAN 21-1 Ch. 5, MSEP write-ups on the 202 process should be eliminated. The automated system also reduces the time it takes to process a 202 compared to the paper process most organizations currently use. Allows more timely support from the SPO's, ensure maintenance activities follow correct procedures, provide visibility of 202s to maintenance, engineering and management, and supply data to the SPO's. investmentDescription: The Deployable Disbursing System (DDS) is a Disbursing application developed by the Defense Finance and Accounting Service (DFAS) and is the SDI-T (Standard Disbursing Initiative - Tactical) solution. DDS is also the DoD end state solution for Disbursing.  DDS is an integrated disbursing system managing disbursing officers accountability and reporting transactional information to Treasury. DDS is the US sole Disbursing System utilized by Army, Navy and US Marine Corps and is also the ERP for the USMC.  DDS was developed as a joint effort between the Directorate of Accounting and Finance Systems and Procedures and the Directorate for Technical Services Organization, located at the DFAS - Indianapolis. DDS is a disbursing system that will meet several goals and customer bases. DDS will produce date in financial statements and bring financial data under general ledger control in accordance with the General Accounting Office, the Joint Financial Management Improvement Plan, the Office of the Management and Budget mandate, and the Financial Management Modernization Plan and will be consistent with the Marine Corps Clean Audit and Financial Improvement Initiative (FII). Exchange transactions allow a cashier or agent the ability to cash checks and perform foreign currency conversions. Both the Treasury's Eagle Cash stored value card, and the check scanning OTCNet applications interface directly with DDS. The exchange process can also be linked to a local customer database that provides the user warnings when the customer has dishonored checks, exceeds an authorized check-cashing limit, or is within set number of days from permanent change of station. DDS indirectly interfaces with several entitlement and accounting systems, to include ERPs. Entitlement systems such as IATS, CAPS and GFEBS will provide a ready to pay file that DDS processes behind the scenes. At the end of the business day, accounting data can be produced for GFEBS, STANFINS, DCAS and E&C. EFT (domestic and international) using ITS and other local formats are used. DDS does have the capability to split disbursement for travel pay between the Government credit card and travelers. DDS will also create the SF1149 and SF 1179 for all check payments that are made. The accountability reports produced are the DD1081 *Statement of Agent Officer's Account), SF 1219 (Statement of Accountability), DD 2657 (Daily Statement of Accountability), and DD 2665 (Daily Agent Accountability Summary).

investmentDescription: The Defense Disbursing Analysis Reporting System (DDARS) reports, validates, and reconciles DFAS disbursement data for U.S. Treasury reporting.  As a centralized repository for disbursement and accounting data, DDARS validates, routes, tracks and controls disbursement and accounting transactions reported by and for Defense Agencies Accounting business line - Columbus and Indianapolis sites. DDARS validates appropriation data and routes transactions to designated accounting operations teams for processing into one of several accounting systems.  Processed accounting transactions are then fed into DDARS and systemically matched and reconciled. Unreconciled transactions are manually researched and corrected as appropriate.  Requests for Information (RFIs) are tracked and aged within the system for internal audit and reporting purposes.  DDARS provides consolidated Treasury RCS-302 reporting to DFAS Indianapolis for Disbursing Station Symbol Numbers 6355 and 6551 on a monthly basis. In addition, it provides Defense Cash Accountability System (DCAS) a consolidated daily file of Columbus disbursement data for processing into their system. investmentDescription: The Standard Contract Reconciliation Tool (SCRT) automates and streamlines the contract reconciliation process. It's designed to accept and format data from external organizations and provides a central point of communication facilitating the team reconciliation process and eliminating duplicate efforts. It provides the central registry of contracts being reconciled within DoD, identifying the person responsible for reconciliation. This eliminates duplication of effort, i.e. 2 organizations reconciling the same contract. SCRT consists of the following components: Registration - allows users to register a new contract, look up registration status of an existing contract, assign/edit team members, and review adjustments made to previously closed reconciliations. Compare - inspects data between systems and alerts users to any discrepancies or adverse situations. Adjustments - allows users to make adjustments to data encountered during the Compare process. An audit trail tracks adjustments made and the responsible parties involved. Manual Input - allows users to enter data not available via automated systems. Reports - allows users access to data for research or to be used as supporting documentation. SCRT interfaces with six accounting systems and Mechanization of Contract Administrative Services (MOCAS).

investmentDescription: The primary function of the MyAirForceBenefits website is to meet the requirements of the National Defense Authorization Acts which require the creation of a readily accessible, web-based benefit information program for all Surviving Spouses, Service members and their Families. The NDAA requires a public facing site for Family members and Survivors to access. Additionally, active duty and reserve Airmen require access to a benefits information program when not on duty, not at a govt facility, or not on a govt computer. The website automates and provides self-service capabilities for many tasks associated with the delivery, management, and day-to-day functions associated with Airmen & Family Readiness Programs. As of today, the U.S. Air Force is finally in compliance with these NDAA mandates, as it now has a readily accessible web-based benefit and counseling information program for all Airmen, including a reliable SBP automated calculator, and an automated military retirement calculator. The website provides thousands of Air Force Airmen across all Components, and their Family members, full access to military benefits information, and provide surviving Family members from all Services (both active and inactive service member deaths) with tailored benefits reports using information validated by the Service Casualty/Survivor staff.  Additionally, the website provides hundreds of SBP counselors around the world with vital automated tools to help them conduct their counseling and estimate calculation duties daily. Primary beneficiaries are Total Force Airmen and their Family member dependents around the world. Project management for the website is achieved through collaboration between the Air Force, AFPC/DP0BB, IT Business Services, IT Business Analysis and the U.S. Army, Retirement Services Office, Soldier for Life Directorate of Military Personnel Management, Office of the Deputy Chief of Staff, G-1. investmentTitle: Air Force MILPERS Integrated Data and Analytics System
investmentDescription: The current MILPERS stand-alone data repository and budget modeling tool was created more than 10 years ago using then available Cognos version 7, MS Windows Server 2003, and MS Excel software. This now obsolete, legacy software platform is beyond end-of-life support by vendors and does not meet current information technology (IT) and security standards, and therefore, is not authorized for hosting within the AF IT network. The absence of AF IT network and vendor software support results in extensive and costly reliance upon contractor support for day-to-day operation and maintenance of the current standalone data repository and budget modeling tool. To remedy the impending software concerns and ensure the AF meets DoD, Office of Management and Budget (OMB) and Congressional budgetary requirements, the AF requires a replacement stand-alone data repository and budget modeling tool, brand name or equal to Board. This Board brand name or equal tool will store current and prior-year execution data as well as include a future-years formulation segment, pricing and costing components, and a J-Book output system. The new tool will be utilized and hosted on the AF network, therefore significantly reducing future reliance on contractor support. This data repository and budget modeling tool will be used exclusively by MILPERS budget offices within the AF Total Force (TF) Component, which consists of: Regular AF (RegAF), Air National Guard (ANG) and AF Reserve (AFR). The AF?s objective in utilizing this data repository and budget modeling tool is to improve the accuracy and level of detail of the entire programming and budget formulation process, to include the pricing and costing of future requirements and the retrieval of current year and historical execution.

investmentDescription: The Commanders? Resource Integration System (CRIS) is a centralized read only data repository of U.S. Air Force financial budget and execution, supply, and personnel and payroll data, populated by standard legacy systems. It allows users to see daily business transactions anywhere in the world at any time, with some transactions updated multiple times a day (near real time). With CRIS, users can design and submit their own queries, allowing them to retrieve exactly the data that they need to see. This ad hoc capability gives users the ability to receive only the data that is relevant to their question, enabling them to make more informed decisions.  CRIS utilizes a virtualized cloud environment reducing hardware and data center footprint while maintaining high levels of performance. In addition, CRIS uses a Service Oriented Architecture (SOA) best practice in that it eliminates the need for point-to-point data links and utilizes web services as a method of server communication. CRIS is built on a cloud scale out architecture using integrated commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) software products including Microsoft? SQL Server?, EntelliCache?, and EntelliFusion? Studio. The software components that make up the architecture are loosely coupled allowing for operating system, Relational Database Management System (RDBMS), and other COTS software patches and upgrades to take place without the need to make changes to CRIS. This architecture provides the ability to be deployed across multiple RDBMS instances. CRIS is many instances of Microsoft? SQL Server databases federated to support a single scaled out application. CRIS uses Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) and Common Access Card (CAC) to restrict access to the system to authorized users only or other systems having DOD-issued certificates.  To ensure data security, CRIS employs a common security model involving the use of roles within the system. Using the Management Console application, functional program office (SAF/FM AFFSO) personnel can define and apply roles to user accounts that define the data to which the user is granted access. Using these centrally managed roles allows the restriction of information sets (such as CivPay, DJMS etc.) to the organization.

This technology offers a ?human in the loop? machine learning and optimization solution to dramatically speed up the weaponeering process. investmentDescription: APPLICATION. SILC software application is designed to improve productivity in US Army ammunition inventory management operations. SILC is used at various ammunition depots and ammunition supply points to assist with ammunition inventory management operations.  This application has two primary functions:  1) to enhance user productivity during the physical inventory process and 2) to automatically reconcile the actual physical inventory with the LMP records.  SILC interfaces with Logistics Modernization Program (LMP) for receiving custodial balances and sending reconciled balances and discrepancies to LMP through an interface. It produces an output file that is used for updating the stock record in the LMP. For label printing, SILC utilizes information extracted from the existing stock record. Operators select the building where the items are located, highlight the item(s) for which a label is required, and specify the number of labels required. Physical inventory is gathered using a hand-held scanner and the inventory information is transferred to a compact disk (CD). SILC reads the CD and compares the scanned inventory with the existing inventory record and performs reconciliation. It informs users of any discrepancies that need to be researched and/or investigated. SILC is loaded on a laptop. Each day the user takes the laptop to the ammunition storage facilities (igloos) that are often remote areas miles away from the home office. The user researches the discrepancies at the igloo. If any discrepancies are found, they are worked at the igloo and new labels are printed if needed. When the user returns to the home office at the end of the day, SILC produces an output file that is copied to a CD. The CD is used to update the LMP application. SILC allows JMC to be in compliance with the following regulations (DOD 4140.1-R, AR 190-11, and AMC-R 740.27).  No additional capabilities.

investmentDescription:
CIS-NCR is the cornerstone of the Office of Chemical Safety and Pollution Prevention (OCSPP), Toxic Substance Control Act (TSCA) chemicals program.  All data and documents collected under TSCA regulations are submitted into and processed through the system.  The system also contains products generated during Agency reviews.
CIS-NCR is housed in 2 environments.  Data collection applications (frontend) are housed in the Central Data Exchange (CDX).  There are currently 18 applications collecting data under all regulated sections of TSCA.  Each application is designed in a dynamic manner to enhance and simplify user experience by showing displaying only required elements based off data entered or options selected by the user.  Embedded validations within each application also help ensure all information is correctly captured and display messages to users when required elements are missing or do not match required formats.  The applications allow users collaborate with others both within and outside their companies to build their data packages over a period, instead of requiring all data and documents to be entered at one time.
Submitted data packages are migrated to backend systems housed in the OPPT Confidential Business Information (CBI) LAN.  This data is transferred in an encrypted state in a point-to-point manner ensuring the security and confidentiality of the information.
The systems contained in the CBI LAN collect and store data and documents submitted by industry and work products generated by federal staff during the review and processing of the submitted information.  Components of the backend systems include databases which store the fielded (structured) submission and staff work product data, workflows for the prescreening, processing, and review of TSCA submissions, chemical reviews, risk assessments and risk management activities, document storage systems for submitted and internal work products, reporting and dashboarding tools, chemical modeling tools, processes for the review of confidentiality claims, a secure communication functions that allow staff to send confidential information and documents to submitters, via CDX, in a secure manner, processes for 100% electronic fee collection, and a process to publish non-CBI/sanitized information  to the public website ChemView to support transparency.

investmentDescription: AFRL DP uses GOTS C2S2 to manage AFRL Lab Demo personnel's pay, performance & other personnel related items for 12 years.  The data base is used by Supervisors & AFRL/DP personnel in all matters relating to the Lab Demo program. Lab Demo personnel are distributed throughout AFRL so supervisory personnel (both Military & Civilian) access/update data from across AFRL.  It  is a software application that has on-line (web-based) and off-line components that supports administration of Lab pay for performance system including conducting appraisals, setting pay, and managing position documents.  It Enforces business processes & business rules that comprise three major components of the demo: contribution-based compensation system, & simplified classification.  Below highlight various aspects of the software: Maintain data on each employee that is critical for the CCS process.  Much of it is not the DCPDS (supervisory structure, job category, pay pool, time in demo, etc.), so a separate database is necessary. "Freeze" the status of all employees as of 30 September each year. All CCS decisions are based on status of the workforce as of that date.  All statements of duties and experience (which replaced Position Descriptions) are developed & maintained in C2S2.  SDE data elements are linked to employee records. All supervisors record their narrative descriptions of each employee's contribution on all six factors each year. They also enter category scores for each factor.  This provides an archive of appraisals and a search able database that can be used to measure status of each appraisal cycle. A key component of CCS is the meeting of managers in which scoring standards are normalized across supervisors & numeric rating are assigned.  C2S2 supports this complex process with automated tools, both on-line and off-line and is the direct link between contribution scores & pay.  The math is complex & the rules are tricky. C2S2 also supports this process by providing pay pool managers with on-line & off-line tools that do math & enforce rules. Once appraisal &  pay setting processes are complete, C2S2 generates transactions that update DCPDS & the payroll system and generates feedback forms that are signed by supervisors & given to employees to record their contribution scores & the resulting pay adjustments.  C2S2 also tracks mid-cycle feedback to ensure that it is accomplished in a timely manner.  The system does not meet the criteria for Internal Use Software (IUS).

investmentDescription: A series of policies across the Federal Government, Department of Defense (DoD), and the Department of Navy (DON) have been developed to increase cloud adoption in an effort to yield cost efficiencies, leverage innovative technology, and decrease reliance on traditional on-premise data center infrastructure. Within the Navy, the DON Chief Information Officer (CIO) released a memo entitled ?Acquisition and Use of Commercial Cloud Computing Services? in 2015, with follow-up guidance released on May 17, 2016 that established a ?Cloud Forward? mentality across the Navy Enterprise. Within the policy, a Cloud First goal was set to move 75% of Navy Information Technology (IT) capabilities (systems, applications, and services) to the commercial environment by 2022.  In February 2017, the Department of the Navy Deputy Chief Information Officer (DDCIO (N)) released a ?Cloud First? memo that further communicated the Navy?s commitment to leverage commercial cloud services in place of on premise, government-owned hosting facilities. The premise of this policy guidance and being Cloud Forward within the Navy is to utilize cloud services as a primary option, if it fits within the business need of a mission owner. Per the DDCIO (N) Navy Commercial Cloud Brokerage Policy, dated Dec 19, 2017, Naval Facilities Engineering Command (NAVFAC) is a designated Navy Cloud Broker (NCB). The primary responsibility of the NCB is to allow Navy consumers to contract, consume, and manage authorized commercial cloud services. Navy PEO-EIS, PMW 270 under the Navy Commercial Cloud Services (NCCS) Program is the Executive Agent (EA) providing leadership and guidance to all NCBs.

investmentDescription: The Air Force Safety Automated System (AFSAS) automates the mishap, hazard, and incident reporting/investigation process, provides a single Air Force (AF) repository for all safety data, and a complete cross functional knowledge base for analysis and trending. It saves lives and DOD assets by implementing effective policy and through active mishap analysis and prevention management, provides the analysis and reporting vehicle. AFSAS is a globally accessible system used by all authorized Air Force and DOD personnel for reporting mishaps over the web. The system provides mishap incident management in accordance with business rules outlined in Air Force Instruction 91-204, "Safety Investigation and Reports" and DoDI 6055.07 Accident Investigation, Reporting, and Record Keeping. It provides Commanders and Senior Leaders, both in the field and at HAF, all the information necessary to make informed decisions regarding safety improvements for reducing mishaps, preserving AF assets, and saving lives. The AFSAS system automates the mishap reporting/investigation process, provides a single AF repository for all safety data, provides a complete cross functional knowledge base for analysis and trending, provides timely risk mitigation data to Air Force decision makers, and integrates Operational Risk Management into all mission activities.  AFSAS is being transformed to enhance discovery of risk factors contributing to mishaps providing a more comprehensive safety management system. AFSAS provides the following benefits: Preserves mission combat capability by saving lives and protecting assets; Improves data accuracy/accessibility, messaging and communication; Guides mishap investigation and OSHA reporting process; Raises confidence levels in mishap causal identification and prevention recommendations; Standardizes Air Force Safety technology solution and provides proactive safety capabilities for the Airman to leverage, enabling mishap prevention and hazard mitigation. There are no dependencies or earlier incarnations of AFSAS. The investment is utilized by USAF, COCOMS, DeCA, DIA, DCMA, the Smithsonian, NASA, DFAS, DHA, US Navy, and USCG. AFSAS is managed and operated daily by the Analysis & Cyberspace Operations Division (SEA). SEA develops and sustains the Air Force Safety Automated System (AFSAS), which collects and maintains data for mitigating mishaps for all safety disciplines in the Air Force.

It is used to store collected trend data, audit trail messages, alarm and event messages, and annotations.  The LCS servers are a specialized ethernet-based supervisory controller that manages field level building automation devices
that typically control and monitor Heating Ventilation and Air Conditioning (HVAC) equipment, meters, lighting, security, fire, and building access.  The LCS provides features including alarm and event management, trending, energy management, scheduling, and password protection.  The LCS uses the LON over IP network communication protocols.
