investmentDescription: The Department of Defense Trauma Registry (DoDTR) implemented the 2004 Assistant Secretary of Defense for Health Affairs directive to capture, maintain, and report all battlefield injury demographics, care, and outcomes for both military and civilian casualties. Recognizing the success and enduring need for DoDTR to support Readiness Capabilities DoDI 6040.47 issued in 2016 (1) establishes policy, assigns responsibilities, and provides procedures to develop and maintain an enduring global trauma care capability that supports a full range of military operations, including a comprehensive DoD Trauma Registry; (2) recognizes the JTS as a DoD Center of Excellence (DCoE); (3) establishes an integrated Combatant Command (CCMD) Trauma System (CTS) requirement modeled after the CENTCOM Joint Theater Trauma System (JTTS); and (4) establishes a requirement to input data into the DoDTR to support unique CCMD mission requirements. The DoDTR is a web-based system with integrated medical specialty modules that provides a vehicle to host and analyze all battlefield casualty data. It hosts trauma-related data collected throughout the entire continuum of care from the point of injury through long term rehabilitative care at medical treatment facilities (MTF). As a web-based system it enables the collection of day-to-day trauma related care from all the deployed, OCONUS and CONUS MTFs. This includes the follow-on care provided to those with battlefield injuries. It also maintains integrated medical specialty registries for collecting additional and relevant medical data to improve combat medical doctrine, provide actionable medical information, enable system-wide trauma Process Improvement, assist materiel developers with requirements and analysis, enhance medical training, and provide relevant data for medical studies and help direct research needs.

The KaRL system does not actively solicit, directly or indirectly, PII for collection. The potential presence of PII in the KaRL system is as a by-product of the R&D records that are generated within the organization as a part of day-to-day operating activities. The PII elements, which are a by-product, is employment information; home/cell phone; mailing/home address; official duty address; place of birth; work email address; birth date; education information; official duty telephone; personal email address; position/title; rank/grade; security information; DOD ID number; emergency contact; name(s)/other names used; photo(s).

investmentDescription: APPLICATION -AOAP Related Publications AR 700-132, Joint Oil Analysis Program AR 750-1, Army Material Maintenance Policy AMCR 11-47, Army Oil Analysis Program OASIS will not be consumed by GCSS-Army. The Oil Analysis Standard Inter-service System (OASIS) is a Software Application that is used as part of an Object Relational Database Management System or Army and Navy Oil Analysis Laboratories worldwide.  It uses an Oracle Database Server as part of its backend database to process store and report on results of analytical test data from various oil analysis test instruments.  The software application is designed to interface seamlessly with the Logistics Information Warehouse (LIW). Each component in the database has a unique default view providing the physical science technicians a user-friendly visual detection environment of problem trends. The hardware requirements are standard personal computer workstations and servers using the Microsoft Windows Vista Professional Operating Software and Vista AGM. The main users are the laboratory physical science technicians .Benefits - Reduce maintenance cost, conserve petroleum products and extend component life. Engineering community and original equipment manufacturers use the data to influence engineer design and improve equipment reliability. The OASIS receives input of oil sample information provided by customer units detailing the oil wetted components and major end item serial numbers and other traceable information. The results of the analytical instruments are automatically transferred to the database and the graphical user interface displays the results. All data is seamlessly transferred to the LIW. The final output is provided to the war-fighter and decision makers in near real time via the web in the form of reports and in the near future, dashboards.- No additional functionality- Additional capabilities- Determine type/amount of wear metals, oil health, viscosity, contamination, and trend.- Enforce consistency in lab sample processing.- Improve readiness by detecting impending failures in critical components.- Enforce component guidelines and limits.- Provide warfighters with a web interface to monitor activity.

investmentTitle: HQ AFPC Intelligent Contact Management System
investmentDescription:
General Description:   The HQ AFPC ICMS is a Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) system which provides telephony services to the Air Force Personnel Center.  This system provides basic telephony services (ingoing / outgoing voice and voicemail) to over 3000 users.  In addition to the basic telephony services it provides to the general populace, it also provides the contact center telephony management for the Total Force Service Center (TFSC).  Currently using Cisco Call Managers and Genesys Telephony Routing, this system provides the capabilities of agent determination, agent skilling, skills-based routing, Intelligent Voice Response and queuing in support of the TFSC mission.  This system is completely isolated on the JBSA-Randolph enclave, with no external data connections.  Inbound and outbound telephony are delivered to the JBSA-Randolph DMS which is the gateway for all calls (DSN and commercial).  The utilization of a media gateway converts the calls from PSTN to VoIP within the AFPC network.


Functional Considerations.  This system supports C2 users and is connected to the DSN but not to the PTSN.  The external DSN connection from this system occurs at the host-base DMS 100 for conversion to an analog signal.  While the DSN is used within AFPC to communicate with world-wide customers, VoIP is not direct from AFPC to the DSN.  It is internal to Randolph only.  This system currently meets Joint Staff certification requirements, all equipment is JITC certified and can be found on a DISA APL.  The ICM servers are housed in a secure facility on the second floor of AFPC (D2E).  Access to the area is controlled by two swipe card access systems that require a PIN.  All technical users and administrators of the system have met all IA requirements and have proper clearances to manage the system.  The DISA VoIP Security Readiness Review and Cisco Router checklists have been run against the implementation and security configurations for this system meets or exceeds all requirements.

investmentDescription: Army Test and Evaluation Command (ATEC) Integrated Mission Management System (AIMMS) is a proposed replacement for the legacy ATEC Decision Support System (ADSS) (DITPR ID #1201) and Versatile Information Systems Integrated On-line Nationwide (VISION) (DITPR ID #1202).  These systems are decades old, built on obsolete technologies, and designed for a previous ATEC organizational structure and business processes that have since changed, forcing many costly system modifications over the years.  Generations of code changes by a series of developers introduced reliability and maintainability problems and cybersecurity vulnerabilities.  AIMMS will enable test officers and evaluators to initiate, plan, manage, analyze, and report on test and evaluation (T&E) projects.  AIMMS will enable leadership to monitor and provide oversight of the execution of the T&E mission, and permit evaluators and other Army, Joint, and DoD stakeholders to easily search, discover, access, and analyze T&E-related information in connected systems throughout ATEC.  AIMMS will provide a unified, reliable, user-friendly, and secure capability to create, store, locate, retrieve, analyze, manage, and share all types of T&E information, from project initiation through archival and close out, including:  Data collected during testing (both instrumentation-generated and manually collected), Assessment and evaluation reports generated from test data, and Project management information and metrics such as plans, schedules, costs (estimated and actual), and reports.   ATEC?s vision for AIMMS is to create an integrated T&E mission workplace for the planning, execution, reporting, and evaluation of T&E activities for all the mission capability areas that ATEC supports.  AIMMS will:  Save time and labor associated with executing manual processes to enter information into and retrieve data from multiple individual, siloed systems; Better align with current ATEC business processes and easily adapt as processes evolve; Provide advanced search capabilities across all T&E data repositories; Provide workspaces for project execution and collaboration; and Foster confidence in records management by providing the ability to trace document to source data, approvals, and distribution.  AIMMS will be the authoritative source of detailed T&E cost and performance data, provide transparency and auditability of project information, and provide the ability to locate any T&E data or documents anywhere in ATEC.

investmentDescription: NOAH is a system used by the audiology community to perform basic hearing aid fitting, analysis of audiograms, speech or loudness tests and has the capability to create journal entries in each patient record. NOAH is comprised of integrated tools, referred herein as modules, developed and maintained by multiple suppliers within the HIMSA community. Patient data is stored to a central database and can be read by any of the approved and tested modules within the accredited NOAH system. The Hearing Center of Excellence (HCE) is transitioning NOAH from a stand-alone configuration at each military treatment facility to an enterprise solution with one common database to store patient data. Upon approval of the NOAH v4.12 baseline, sites currently using a previous version of NOAH will be upgrading to a FIPs 140-2 compliant, CAC enabled version connected to a centralized hosting environment on the Medical Community of Interest MedCOI) network. The NOAH v4.12 environment is comprised of one centralized server and multiple clients within 100+ audiology clinics across DHA. The NOAH SQL DB (SQL Cluster) provides database resources for the clients to store patient information relative to audiology. The server uses a Microsoft Windows Server 2016 operating system and Microsoft SQL Server 2016 as the database engine, both hosted within the DHA Compute Storage Management System (CSMS) Hosting Enclave. The end clients will be installed Standard Desktop Configured (SDC) Windows 10 imaged workstation procured and provided by the military treatment facility (MTF) with a connection to the NOAH application server over the network, thereby sharing a common database architecture. Sustainment of the NOAH system is accomplished through the Application Virtualization Hosting Environment (AVHE), a centralized remote administration model utilizing the CITRIX-ICA-SSL/TLS service, which allows the HCE PMO remote access for system testing and sustainment. The CITRIX-ICA-SSL/TLS service encrypts all data passing between the server and client by utilizing SSL encryption. NOAH is FIPS 140-2 compliant, utilizing the crypto functionality of the underlying operating system (OS), along with supporting Two Factor Authentication (2FA).

investmentTitle: Processing Evaluating and Reporting of Force Management Data Software
investmentDescription: The Processing Evaluating and Reporting of FORce Management Data Software (PERFORMS) is a weapons systems lifecycle management and engineering toolset which processes the F-16 Crash-Survivable Flight Data Recorder (CSFDR) files and provides data for related Aircraft Structural Integrity Program (ASIP) engineering analysis. PERFORMS has evolved into an integral F-16 resource for the sustainment engineer through the generation of reports and inspection requirements necessary to maintain the structural integrity of the F-16 fleet.  PERFORMS is used daily as the sole processing tool for F-16 flight recorder data, providing ASIP flight data validation and standardization.  As a sustainment engineering tool, PERFORMS broadens the scope of capabilities to both a macro view of the F-16 fleet and a micro view of individual aircraft. PERFORMS calculates cumulative lifetime flight severity for each individual aircraft, then levies a tail number-specific maintenance inspection due at a defined flight hour. The data created by PERFORMS is critical to the F-16 fleet, which is used in conjunction with robust structural integrity resources, flight severity comprehension, and engineering expertise to ensure continued availability of individual F-16 aircraft. PERFORMS operates independently as a server-based tool to process and report flight data. This processed data is used to determine individual structural inspection requirements, which are then communicated to the field units through the Individual Aircraft Tracking app within F-16 ASIP Portal.

investmentDescription: The AMCOM Safety Messages (ASM) enables the AMCOM Safety Office (ASO) to perform flight safety message issuance across weapon systems. investmentTitle: Facilities and Equipment Maintenance Web Interface
investmentDescription: FEMWEB is a server based web application, utilizing Window's Internet Information Services. It is available to anyone with a CAC on the Tinker-2k network. It is used as a reporting tool for FEM, provides information from the FEM database to Tinker and Tinker PMEL customers, engineers, and management in the form of dynamic, interactive reports on the condition and status of equipment and tools without a FEM account and without FEM software being installed, ability to create functions that assist OC-ALC customers, maintainers, and management, refines requirements for the command system's maintainers. Using FEMWEB resolves the need to manage FEM accounts and FEM training to the approximately 24,000 Air Force maintainers and support personnel at Tinker by generating customized, intuitive, job function oriented web pages that provide real time, authoritative data from the AF Command FEM system which are supplemented with locally designed and maintained data sets not currently in FEM but immediately needed by maintainers and management. This local development capability not only enhances maintenance flexibility but also provides professional and reliable data design and management which serves as a requirement prototyping tool for FEM and also allows existing minor maintenance functions a 'no cost' resource for computerized data management where no option currently exists. The benefits to the mission are: Reduced confusion caused by incorrectly user defined reports and rapid application development capabilities to accommodate site specific issues that could take years to acquire in the Command Standard System, FEM. Additionally, FEMWEB allows Tinker personnel to develop and refine system specifications before the initial design has been submitted to the FEM developer, dramatically reducing turn-around time as compared to processing initial subsequent design specifications strictly through the Command Standard process. Tinkers FEMWEB team (also supports daily operation) is the same group of IT professionals that support and maintain the FEM system at Tinker AFB allowing this team to make informed decisions on how to best accommodate Tinker business needs. FEMWEB developers create administrative applications that are used by OC-ALC, in FEMWEB, for supervisors and employees to monitor and maintain daily administration functions in real time to better support OC-ALC, and importantly the war fighter.

It also allows users to enter issues and comments related to specific part numbers and quantities.  The system contains over 80 user screens, and over 60 tailored reports. investmentDescription: By DOD directive, the services are required to collect medical event reports (MERs) for over 70 specific medical diagnoses and events and forward these reports to the AFHSC for DOD-wide collation.  These events are reportable due to: their mission degrading potential, our ability to prevent the illness by establishing specific control measures, and/or their potential for rapid spread causing significant outbreaks.    DRSi is a web-based tool designed to be easy to use (with minimal training for users), flexible (to rapidly accommodate additional information needs for emerging public health concerns), and transparent (allowing access to critical information at the local, regional, and higher headquarters level as soon as a report is entered into the electronic system).  DRSi is accessed through a secured website.  The data are stored at NMCPHC in a SQL environment.    To support disease surveillance and response needs, Personally identifiable Health Information (PHI) is collected in DRSi and is stored in the back-end database.  Therefore, user access is restricted.  Users must fill out a System Authorization Access Request (SAAR) form for access, endorsed by someone in their chain of command with by-direction authority.  Signatures are then verified before users are provided account access.   As account holders, units providing inpatient or outpatient care log into DRSi and fill out a Medical Event Report (MER) for a reportable event.  In the MER, information specific to public health control measures (such as travel history, vaccine history, and chemoprophylaxis) is filled out by the local medical or preventive medicine department.  MER information is then used to track illnesses and trends across the local or regional area as well as enterprise-wide.

The SECAF directed AF Materiel Command to partner with BA Major Commands to provide BA with full life-cycle acquisition management of equipment, ensure interoperability of common use BA equipment, and capitalize on opportunities for synergies across BA mission areas (per AFPD 10-35 4.3). Currently, BA procurement processes often take more than 120 days and result in multiple shipments with a location as the only defined recipient; a significant shortfall when one location may have 80 members.  The processes do not allow for kitting of equipment.  Gear distribution and accountability can drive a significant burden on the units for large orders.  In addition, the processes do not allow for the required level of standardization and individual accountability controls.  Significant delays in equipment issue have resulted in Battlefield Airmen Rapid Refresh and Replenishment (BARS) users not being fully mission capable.  Inadequate equipment for BA has recently been brought to the CSAF attention and he directed every piece of BA equipment should be provided quickly and treated with the same sensitivity as aircrew equipment.  AF/A3 has identified BARS and associated processes as the solution. BARS will provide an interface for efficiently ordering kits and/or individual equipment items from approved standardized listings.  The system will be accessible via the internet.  BARS will interface with a pre-stocked supply point to efficiently deliver individual equipment items or kits to BA, AFOSI and EOD Human Weapon Systems. ACC OPR:  A3/A3JO; SPO:  AFLCMC/WISN; SW Sustainment - 580 SMXS.

investmentDescription:
The Assignment Management System (AMS) consists of the three main components: (1) AMS Web Application, (2) Millennium Windows Application, and (3) Base-Level Service Delivery Model (BLSDM) Web Application. These applications support officer assignments, enlisted assignments, commander responsibilities, individual active duty Air Force members, aviator retention pay, and base level personnel actions.
AMS encompasses the assignment processes for all active duty officers (from 2nd Lieutenant through Lieutenant Colonel) and enlisted (Airman First Class through Chief Master Sergeant) into one system. The system provides Air Force Personnel Center, Directorate of Assignments, the capability to advise airmen of potential positions, select individuals for assignment, and advise both selected and non-selected members concerning assignment selections. Users have access to a portion of the system so they view their own personnel data, the ability to use manning tools, volunteer for available assignments, and review career field information. AMS includes the Aviator Retention Pay (ARP) functionality which automates the ARP agreement application process for the Air Force ARP Program for the Active Duty Component. ARP provides a monetary bonus to rated active duty officers for their continued service in the Air Force. The ARP is used to allow eligible active duty officers to apply for the program and for the Business Process Owner (BPO) to process their ARP agreements.
Millennium is a Windows application that supports AMS. Millennium is used by the BPOs to manage officer assignment selections. Millennium encompasses the assignment selection process for all active duty officers (from 2nd Lieutenant through Lieutenant Colonel). The application provides the BPO the capability to advise service members of potential positions, select individuals for assignment, and advise both selected and non-selected members concerning assignment selections. The application does not support Guard or Reserve positions.
 BLSDM provides commanders and their delegates the capability to retrieve queries and request personnel actions on AF members within their unit, group or wing. The application provides commanders the capability to produce a wide variety of pre-defined and user-driven personnel data reports with manpower and personnel data from the Military Personnel Data System (MilPDS). In addition, it provides the capability to export these reports to Microsoft Excel.

investmentDescription: Flight Operations Management (Flight Ops) combines scheduling, training, and standardizations/evaluations applications, supporting AMC and ACC sortie scheduling. This is the enterprise solution optimizing the unit?s human and materiel resources in the operations schedule to maximize the value of each sortie and increase total force readiness to maximize wing lethality. Flight Ops will increase tactical readiness, reduce total number of training sorties required to maintain currencies, and reduce time required for operator upgrades by optimizing aircrew scheduling assignments and integrating with complementary problem space solutions to provide seamless data flow that accelerates Air Force (AF) operational and strategic decision making. Flight Ops will provide an extensible cloud-based Platform as a Service (PaaS) hosting platform built to deliver highly resilient mission planning applications to units and users deployed around the world. Flight Ops will integrate capabilities currently found in the Puckboard and Patriot Excalibur (PEX) products, enable transition from legacy systems to a system of systems with modernized capabilities. Puckboard is a next-generation application focused on automating crew/mission/sortie scheduling by matching operations to missions based on currencies and crew rest constraints. The application currently has 33,000 users on-boarded, with approximately 12,000 using the application daily. Puckboard?s front and back-end micro-services architecture are hosted via Platform One PaaS Party Bus Value Stream through the Department of Defense (DoD) certified Continuous Authority to Operate (cATO) and Continuous Integration / Continuous Delivery (CI/CD) pipelines and Kubernetes (K8s) ecosystem. PEX is a software toolset that enables an organization to seamlessly share information and enhance situational awareness by enabling AF, Joint Service, and Foreign Military personnel to perform accurate, real-time operational tasks, track readiness status and connect these functional areas within a unit. PEX supports flying and non-flying, ground, Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR) and special mission units, and Major Commands (MAJCOM) by fusing the full spectrum of multi-domain operations.

investmentDescription: The Aviation Cost Evaluation System (ACES) is a Commander Naval Air Forces (CNAF) web application system that is the joint flying hour cost collection system used by Commander, Naval Air Forces, U.S. Pacific Fleet (COMNAVAIRPAC) and the Commander, Naval Air Forces U.S. Atlantic Fleet (COMNAVAIRLANT). ACES is essential for the effective management of the Naval Flying Hour Program (FHP) (includes Navy and Marine) and for all up-line reporting requirements for the Type Commander staff, subordinate commands and higher authority. ACES functionality covers three major areas: Flying Hour Execution, Budget and Planning. ACES resides on a Win 2003 web/database server. ACES tracks Naval Aviation costs by allowing the input and import of Budget OPTAR Reports, Air Station Flying Hour Cost Reports, and other Type Commander (COMNAVRESFOR and CNATRA) reports. Analysis is accomplished by providing 100 available reports within the system. The database consists of an Oracle Relational Database Management System (RDBMS). ACES is the software utilized to generate the Official Monthly Flying Hour Cost Report to OPNAV (N43). ACES captures all costs incurred in support of the FHP from various sources. This includes all Pacific (PAC) and Atlantic (LANT) aviation squadrons, aircraft carriers, MALS (Marine Aviation Logistic Squadrons), naval air stations and the Type Commander?s headquarters. The flexible functionality of ACES provides the Aviation Type Commanders the tool to answer and fulfill ever-changing reporting requirements and any supporting data requested by the Office of the Chief of Naval Operations (OPNAV) in order to support the FHP for building/defending the budget. The types of non-financial data captured include: flight hours, aircraft #, and gallons consumed by fuel type (i.e., JP4/5/8, Comm, Into Plane). The financial data captured includes: aviation fuel, flight administration, aviation maint, contract obligations; contingency costs, reimbursable costs, and Defense Finance and Accounting Service (DFAS) adjustments. ACES has supported, since 1996, the requirement of producing an Official Monthly Flying Hour Cost report as the source data for OPNAV?s Flying Hour Projection System (FHPS). OPNAV utilizes the FHPS to produce the $6B FHP portion of the DoN budget. ASKIT is used by all Navy and Marine Aviation units to report fuel / squadron maintenance funds, flight hours, gallons expenditures, and aircraft #'s at the unit level. ASKIT data is imported into ACES.

investmentDescription: The Range Facility Management Support System (RFMSS) is the Army?s automated system that supports warfighter training.  It is used for training on all types of weapons and live ammo.  It manages individual, unit and CALFEX training.  It efficiently assists unit commanders to provide realistic training for Soldiers in units and schools world-wide.  RFMSS is a standard, integrated system supporting warfighters in the Army, Navy, USMC, USAR and ARNG. RFMSS automates scheduling of firing ranges and training areas.  RFMSS automates fire desk operations.  RFMSS manages the total range training area through the training of Soldiers in live fire, non-live fire range operations and maneuvers. RFMSS facilitates range, air space, and training area scheduling, management, and operations for Army and joint service events. It includes a training unit submission and range control approval process for scheduling ranges and training areas.  It provides automated warning of safety risks.  It identifies scheduling and environmental conflicts for range control resolution.  It supports incident management, to include automating incident reporting.  RFMSS? fire desk operations include text based and graphics-based modes, to include display of appropriate Surface Danger Zones (SDZs).    A ?visibility tool? will be added in FY12/13 to allow multi-service scheduling of DoD training facilities. The RFMSS at Eglin AFB interfaces with the Air Forces? Center Scheduling Enterprise system to provide live fire training support to the newly arrived 7th Special Forces Group. The RFMSS architecture is optimized for range control environments.  In addition to scheduling via the Local Area Network, RFMSS also uses a centralized web server to allow units to remotely submit scheduling requests via the Internet.  The RFMSS application was developed to assist Firing Range and Land Training Area managers manage firing range and training areas to support the ARFORGEN ready pool concept, and it is fully capable of supporting the Army Chief of Staff?s regionally aligned force concept.  RFMSS interfaces with the Army?s Digital Training Management System (DTMS) that facilitates an organization?s ability to plan, schedule, resource, record and report individual training of Soldiers and collective training in units, brigade and below.

investmentDescription: The Distribution and Allowance (DNA) system is an Oracle Web based system used by the HQ, Army Sustainment Command (ASC) and HQ, Joint Munitions Command (JMC) for maintaining personnel, manpower, and budget information.  As such the system is used across organizational lines to include G1, Manpower, and G8.  G1 has the responsibility for maintaining personnel information for the  commands.  DNA communicates with the JMCs Employee Development System (EDS) and TACOMs Total Employee Development (TED) System that ASC uses for training.  DNA has the capability to track manning documents, appraisal information, awards, acquisition data, security clearance information, key/Emergency Essential (EE) positions and drug testing information.  The system is used to ensure timely actions for upward mobility promotions, Within Grade Increases (WIGI s), performance standards/appraisals, and manning documents for strength accountability.  The system also provides standard and unique reports in order to keep the Command group informed on personnel matters.  Manpower has the responsibility for tracking strength, Table Distribution and Allowance (TDA), and Program Budget Guidance (PBG).  DNA is capable of tracking on-board strength, TDA s, PBG, and monthly execution (Army Management Structure Code (AMSCO), Management Decision Package (MDEP).  These reports assist Manpower in conducting analysis and providing reports to the Command group.  From a G8 perspective, this system is used for tracking budget requirements, pay of people, and Standard Operation Maintenance Army Research and Development System/SOMARDS Job Order Number (SOMARDS/SJON) reporting.  DNA integrates Personnel/Manpower for complete resource tracking/reporting.  This system has the capability to track all of these fields of information, which allows the system to provide several standard reports and/or create unique one of a kind reports for special projects/assignments.  DNA allows for real time reporting of information for our entire command. The DNA system is also used to track this same information for all ASC/JMC off-site locations.  This provides the Commands with total personnel accountability of over 7,000 military and civilians, worldwide for ASC/JMC missions.

investmentDescription: RAPS is an ashore web application that is an automated Logistics Management System used by the Naval Air Warfare Centers, both Aircraft Division and Weapons Division (NAWCAD and NAWCWD) and by the Fuels Division of the Naval Supply Command at Patuxent River Maryland.  The fuel module of RAPS is a feeder system to the Defense Logistics Agency Energy Division (DLA-Energy), Fuels Accounting System (FAS)/Fuels Enterprise System (FES) and the Navy ERP Financial System.  The RAPS fuel module supports funds validation, obligation and goods receipt data collection, local and DLA fuel inventory as well as providing field level fuel reporting.  The Fuels Division uses barcode scanning and relational database technologies for the accurate and timely issuance of fuels.  RAPS is a tool used to record and transfer locally issued fuel data thus eliminating the need for manual fuel chits, and manual data entry into FAS.  These fuel transactions include AVGAS (aviation fueling), heating fuels and MOGAS (vehicle fueling).  The individual locally issued fuel transaction information is fed into FAS on a daily basis.  NAWC financial information is recorded at the individual fuel transaction level and stored in the RAPS database.  The current interface allows the Fuels Division to upload the data elements into FAS that are required to generate an invoice that will be processed via an Interdepartmental Billing (Register 06).  FES assigns a document number to each individual fuel transaction and interfaces it back to RAPS on a daily basis. This document number is appended to the originating individual fuel transaction data stored in the database.  The NAWCs also upload fuel information from FES pertaining to fuelings issued outside of Patuxent River.  All NAWC fuel transactions are interfaced to Navy ERP to establish obligations and goods receipts once financial information has been validated.  RAPS also generates the DD1149 and the DD1348-1A government forms for the purpose of shipping/disposing/turning in of material.  RAPS is a function needed to support the missions of NAWC and the Fuels Division of Navy Supply at Patuxent River.

investmentDescription: a. Overall summary of functions the system performs:- The Non-Destructive Test Equipment (NDTE) is a fully integrated mobile and deployable system comprised of an Automated Inspection System (AIS) installed inside a Hard-sided Expandable Light Air Mobile Shelter (HELAMS). The NDTE inspects Soldier Body Armor Enhanced Small Arms Protective Insert (ESAPI) plates for damage. The heart of the NDTE is the AIS which consists of a Windows XP computer, Matrox X-ray machine, imager power supply, and flat-panel imager engineered to detect cracks in hard ceramic armor ballistic plates, the critical component of the Interceptor Body Armor, at a rate of over 300+ plates per hour. The NDTE is integrated with a conveyor system to load plates and with a reader to capture the Unique Identification (UID) label on the ballistic insert being evaluated. As a plate moves around the conveyor belt, the plate's UID is read, the plate is X-rayed, results associated with the UID and entered into a database, and rejected plates are automatically separated from the accepted plates. The system can also inspect plates without UID labels to determine immediate serviceability. This system automatically populates a database to permit data mining for logistical, operational, and research analyses. The NDTE concept of operation is to be operated in the rear support area by contractor logistics support.  b. Who uses the systems (organizations): PM SPE- Central Issue Facilities (CIF).  c. In general terms, the inputs and outputs of the system: Inputs:  NDTE is a stand-alone system.  It only receives information from the results of scanning ESAPI plates.  d. Outputs:  X-ray image (.jpg) from scanned ESAPI plate, Item Unique Identification (IUID) barcode information from ESAPI plate.

investmentDescription: Efficient disciplinary case management capabilities are needed to enhance the abilities of AF JA personnel to advise CC to carry out responsibility for good order and discipline.  Specifically, requires a case management system to assist JAGs to work, track, and analyze disciplinary actions: (1) across the continuum of disciplinary action, from admin to court; and (2) in time, from date of discovery of misconduct to final disposition. The Air Force employs AMJAMS for JA personnel enterprise wide to manage military justice cases. Due to its age and inflexibility to adapt readily and rapidly to requirement changes, the existing solution does not support the Air Force?s current and future disciplinary case processing needs. Lack of agility has resulted in manual workaround solutions in order to comply with laws, regulations, and policies, an overreliance on manual intervention, and poor data quality for specific requests for information in disciplinary cases (e.g., status of cases throughout the military justice lifecycle, types of disciplinary cases, and decisions outside the military justice lifecycle). These deficiencies have also had the effect of requiring the Air Force to keep information in separate spreadsheets, central repositories, and various other home-grown database systems to work and to manage cases, as well as to meet evolving regulatory reporting compliance and increasing data inquiries from the Headquarters Air Force, the Congress, and the public. The aforementioned related problems are being addressed by the DCMS initiative, led by JA. The goal is to more efficiently and effectively provide the AF with a standardized broad spectrum disciplinary case management solution, providing necessary disciplinary case management, reporting, and visibility for Air Force commanders and legal teams. With DCMS implementation, the Air Force will more fully meet its statutory responsibilities under the UCMJ to fairly and efficiently administer military justice and diligently represent the interests of the AF, victims, and accused Airmen. The determined solution is a modern cloud-hosted, low-code, case management platform which provides strong functionality in the areas of adaptive case handling, content interaction, integration and interoperability, data capture, output management, role-based customized user experience, role-appropriate analytics and data visualization and a sustainable lifecycle.  DCMS provides more robust capability for case disposition.

investmentDescription: Collaborative viewing, scoring, vectoring, and feedback system, enabling both Force Development and Force Management competencies for Active Duty, Air National Guard and Air Force Reserve Airmen. The Reporting module automatically organizes source data into standardized, consistent report formats to replace the process or manually creating repetitive reports. Beyond these generic modules, Rubix also contains modules designed to address very specific information and analytic needs for the users, to include: The Budget and Execution module provides day-to-day tracking of an organizational budget including requirements, allotments, and execution. The POM module assists in capturing the continual changes and feedback during the POM process in a way that is consistent to all stakeholders. investmentDescription:
The 17 TRG requires an academic network that provides students, faculty, and staff IT services that are not available on the AFNET.  NIPRnet proxy settings have greatly restricted the amount and variety of data that can be queried, while bandwidth limitations have made the streaming of industry standard training videos impossible in classrooms.  Unclassified training programs at Goodfellow AFB rely on data, imagery, and videos collected from various public websites for instruction, research, and student development of training products. UTS will provide a reliable, secure, managed, and less restrictive connection to the internet via a commercial Internet Service Provider (ISP) with increased bandwidth and fewer restrictions which will broaden access to valuable public resources, as well as allow streaming of training videos in the classroom.


UTS will provide secure and managed wireless access points (WAPs) in the training classrooms for portable electronic devices (PEDs). Mobile computing devices are quickly becoming a requirement to support certain training missions.  DOD?s vision of utilizing technology in training is rapidly evolving and will rely on wireless access to network resources. The implementation of WAPs within the UTS infrastructure will only allow the use of command authorized devices used for training.
UTS will also enable the Goodfellow AFB/17th Training Group to meet the DOD directive to consolidate data centers.  Currently, each of the IT systems being considered for consolidation are in separate independent facilities.  The DOD directive?s intent is to eliminate these independent sites and merge them into larger Special Purpose Processing Nodes (SPPN).  The DOD directive to consolidate data centers eliminates these independent sites from upgrading hardware or software because they are not part of an approved SPPN.  UTS will bring all standalone unclassified systems under a single certified/accredited network with all servers locatedwithin an approved SPPN.  This consolidation also eliminates the need for special power and heating/air conditioning which results in an annual cost savings.  In addition, the consolidation will centralize network, system, and cybersecurity administration.

Conformance is expected in both the classified and unclassified communities, and further guidance will be forthcoming on specific processes and procedures for the classified architecture development efforts in the Department.  DoDAF conformance is achieved when:  * The data in a described architecture is defined according to the DM2 [Sic. DoDAF Meta-Model] concepts, associations, and attributes.  * The architectural data is capable of transfer in accordance with the PES. [Sic. Physical Exchange Specification]? investmentDescription: The Fort Drum Keyless Entry System (KES) is an asynchronous access control system similar to the card swipe lock systems used in commercial hotels. Initial deployment will be to support Single Soldier Housing on Fort Drum. The system is managed by the Fort Drum Public Works Carpenter Shop. The system consists of a server located in DOIM s server farm (10690) running the Stanley BASIS software and SQL Server, a second server providing the web interface, client machines located in Clark Hall and in SSH Team offices to create keys and accounts for Soldiers using the Stanley BASIS client, a Kiosk in Clark hall for Soldiers to get replacement keys using an Internet Explorer based web application, wireless portal gateways located in the ceilings above the halls in the buildings communicating with the locksets utilizing IEEE 802.15.4, power-over-Ethernet routers to support the portal gateways and locksets on each door which authorize and track entry into rooms. Key control officers authorize key cards for individual Soldiers to access their rooms. The database downloads updated lock information to the appropriate portal gateway and retrieves event logs submitted by the locksets. The room locksets poll the portal gateway at approximately 60 second (this is configurable) intervals to upload event data and retrieve access list changes. The communication between the components of the system is over the Fort Drum Unclassified Installation Campus Area Network (ICAN) but is isolated from normal traffic by assigning it to a unique VLAN. System backups shall be accomplished by a separate tape backup system operated by DOIM. This system implementation responds to the Army Design Standards paragraph 3.5.11 Locks and Locking Devices/ as mandated in Memorandum for the Record signed by ACS Installation Management and dated Dec 11, 2007. The KES will improve key control and security by monitoring connecting a key card with an individual and monitoring the use of the card.

investmentDescription: FACTS is a joint unclassified web-based Automated Information System (AIS) that provides a single, integrated process supporting the clearance of all Department of Defense (DoD) cargo for air movement and facilitates Service transportation funds management and budgeting for all modes of transportation.  The unique functionality within FACTS, coupled with embedded Service specific rules, provides efficient resource utilization and transportation fiscal discipline within the DTS. FACTS operates with six functional business areas: Transportation Management Functionality:  FACTS maintains shipment information for the current plus the past six years (7 years) and provides transportation managers the capability to query data, review system-generated reports, and create Service-unique reports.Funds Management Functionality:  FACTS provides financial managers the ability to establish transportation budgets and controls to track and manage their transportation funds. investmentDescription: The Army Centralized Civilian Human Resources Suite (ACCHRS) is an unregistered child of Electronic Official Personnel File Back-File Conversion (eOPF-BFC) DA 205495 in APMS. The commonality between ACCHRS and eOFP-BFC is both are hardware suites that support non-Army systems.  So it is logical that these two hardware suites be combined in APMS to capture the hardware investments for the non-Army systems in a single APMS entry.  The Electronic Official Personnel Folder Back-File Conversion (eOPF-BFC) is the hardware that supports the eOPF which is an OPM system.  This hardware suite that allows for scanning the hardcopy documents from the Official Personnel Folder (OPF) for Army civilian employees into the eOPF. The Army hardware suite is suffixed with the designation of Back-File Conversion to distinguish it from the OPM system so there will be no rationale to think that the Army eOPF-BFC is redundant with the OPM eOPF.  The ACCHRS is the Army hardware suite for the Defense Civilian Personnel Data System (DCPDS).  ACCHRS is a suite of hardware (monitors, scanners, desktops, notebooks, printers etc) used by the Army Human Resource (HR) Civilian Personnel specialists and managers to perform their daily inherited functional HR management missions. ACCHRS will be fielded at all Army Civilian Human Resources Agency activities on CONUS and OCONUS installations that provide human resources management for Army Appropriated Funds units, Army NAF, Army Corps of Engineers, and the DOD Defense Contract Management Agency.  In summary, neither eOPF nor DCPDS are Army systems therefore they are not registered in APMS.  Likewise, eOPF-BFC and ACCHRS are merely the hardware suites that enable Army personnel to use the two non-Army aforementioned systems.  Neither eOPF-BFC nor ACCHRS require an Authority to Operate (ATO) or a Certificate of Networthiness (CoN).  Both hardware suites share the commonality of supporting non-Army systems.  So it is logical that these two hardware suites be combined in a single APMS entry to capture the hardware investments.

investmentDescription: Sec 117 of Title 10 directed the development of a new readiness reporting system. The 2001 QDR established that the DoD needed a broader range of contingencies to determine operational risk than the Department has traditionally analyzed. DoDD 7730.65, ?Defense Readiness Reporting System? established DRRS as the single readiness reporting system for the Department. DRRS supports the DoD readiness management processes: to assess the readiness of forces assigned to current operations, the Guidance for the Employment of the Force (GEF) directs these forces to report in DRRS. To assess contingency operations, Joint Forces Readiness Review (JFRR) uses DRRS to inform timely, scenario-based readiness assessments on a quarterly basis to identify capability shortfalls and risks associated with assigned missions.   DRRS enables commanders and DoD leaders to plan for and respond to the emerging threats that face our nation in a timely and effective manner. DRRS allows leaders to make faster and better informed decisions. DRRS is the primary means by which Defense components -- Combatant Commands, Services, Agencies and their subordinate elements and units -- report their readiness. The system measures readiness of the Department's components to execute the full range of missions assigned by the Secretary of Defense. The Defense Readiness Reporting System (DRRS) establishes a capabilities-based, adaptive, near real-time readiness information system for DoD. DRRS measures the readiness of military forces and supporting infrastructure to meet missions and goals assigned by the Secretary of Defense. The realization of DRRS required integrating a host of key technologies to achieve an information system that supports distributed, collaborative, and dynamic readiness reporting in addition to continuous tool-based assessment. The primary technical goal was the creation of a highly reliable, secure and integrated networked to consolidate readiness data from the Combatant Commands, Services, and DoD agencies. DRRS environment provides the department with its single cross cutting view of readiness information and its supporting data for forces and support organizations.

The current anti-jam protection is limited to two SMART-T terminals per BCT, division and Corps HQs, leaving battalions vulnerable to being isolated during jamming events.  FY19 funding begins the Army's concentrated effort for near term satellite anti-jam protection.

investmentDescription: Defense Information System for Security (DISS) will improve information sharing capabilities, accelerate clearance-processing timelines, reduce security vulnerabilities, and increase Department of Defense (DoD) security mission capability. The DISS mission is to consolidate the DoD security mission into an Enterprise System that will automate the implementation of improved national investigative and adjudicative standards to eliminate costly and inefficient work processes and increase information collaboration across the community. DISS is currently under development and will replace the Joint Personnel Adjudication System (JPAS) a legacy system. When fully deployed this will be a secure, authoritative source for the management, storage and timely dissemination of and access to personnel with the flexibility to provide additional support structure for future DoD security process growth. When deployed, it will accelerate the clearance process, reduce security clearance vulnerabilities, decrease back-end processing timelines, and support simultaneous information sharing within various DoD entities as well as among a number of authorized federal agencies. DISS will provide improved support to the Insider Threat and Personal Identity programs and will be comprised of capabilities that are currently part of the Joint Personnel Adjudication System (JPAS) and will create a robust and real-time capability for all DoD participants in the Military Departments, and DoD Agencies. It will also include automated records check (ARC) functionality and the creation of an adjudicative case management capability with e-Adjudication functionality. DISS will also provide the following operational capabilities, single point of entry for; personnel security, adjudicative case management, and decision support functionality to all DoD adjudicators. DISS will provide near continuous intra-Central Adjudication Facility (CAF) communications on a web-based enabled platform utilizing a unified architecture with security management.

These personnel use LMR to synchronize emergency response efforts and for critical communications support during dispatch, mobilization, deployment and operations. Without adequate communications capabilities that readily enable coordination, maximize the use of scarce radio spectrum and provide secure voice transmissions, emergency responders and base support personnel would be significantly constrained in their ability to perform key functions.

investmentDescription: POCS is an OSD-P initiative to deploy a common information technology platform to improve international partner outreach and collaboration efforts in a federated environment. The program uses a spiral methodology (making available capabilities as developed), to speed the delivery of open source collaboration technologies the user community. DSCA oversees execution of the research and development of the RIO-PIMS effort, and ensures that the program addresses DoD security cooperation requirements in the context of defense, interagency, and international information sharing and collaboration needs.  POCS effort focuses on improving collaboration, supporting outreach efforts, and enabling communication among the Regional Centers for Security Studies, the COCOMS, DSCA, OSD-P, NATO's Military Cooperation Division, the PfP Consortium of Defense Academies, PfP Partner countries, and other designated communities. It provides DoD and international partner security practitioners a platform to share information, communicate and collaborate, and improve administrative activities. Also provides the ability to form collaborative communities of interest around security issues. POCS facilitates information sharing and knowledge management concepts in accordance with U.S. policy. PIMS, as a part of the NATO Enlargement Facilitation Act of 1996, implements the Congressional endorsement for the modernization of Defense capabilities in eligible PfP countries relative to their telecommunications infrastructure. This support is important to achieve the interoperability/integration outlined in the Guidance for the Employment of the Force. POCS supports internet-based education and collaboration, exercise simulations, and training center requirements.  The Regional Centers Person/Activity Management System (RCPAMS) provides an integrated student and activities management framework that was designed to complement the capabilities of the Security Assistance Network (SAN). investmentDescription:
The function of Army Investigative Enterprise System (AIES) is to serve as the Army?s solution to centralize the personnel security investigation (PSI) submission process.  Its main components are the Personnel Security Investigation Portal (PSIP) front-end and its related Remedy-based workflow back-end.    The PSIP is the mechanism where security managers and human resource specialists submit PSI requests for current and prospective Army personnel.   The primary input to PSIP are investigation requests submitted electronically by a security manager or human resource specialist using the web-based application.  The information completed in PSIP is transferred to the internal Remedy application where the investigation request is validated and initiated for the applicant to complete the investigative form.  Following the applicant completing their form, the form is processed through a rules-based application called eReview.  Once successfully reviewed and accepted, the output of AIES are personnel security/suitability investigation requests submitted to the National Background Investigation Bureau (NBIB) formerly the Office of Personnel Management (OPM). 

The Aberdeen Proving Ground Regional Network Enterprise Center (APG-RNEC) hosts the Army Investigative Enterprise System (AIES) and its components.

investmentDescription: The Defense Civilian Personnel Data System (DCPDS) is the Department?s enterprise civilian Human Resources (HR) automated system that supports one-third of the federal work force. Network operations span worldwide and are online 24/7. DCPDS architecture is standardized for all enterprise servers and all Military Departments and Defense Agency regional platforms and uses commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) hardware and software. DCPDS has migrated to Oracle?s Release 12 software, ensuring the technology base to maintain DCPDS as a continued leader in federal HR systems.  Web-enabled DCPDS and the addition of its Self Service capability have increased the number of users from 20,000 HR specialists to over 800,000 DoD employees. Led by the Defense Manpower Data Center (DMDC) DCPDS manager, the Department has been designated by Office of Personnel Management/Office of Management and Budget (OPM/OMB) as one of six (6) HR Shared Service Centers. DCPDS has proved its business case and saves the Department over $200 million per year by operating centrally those HR system activities previously operated by the individual Services/Defense Agencies. DCPDS operational activities include processing of all personnel transactions, providing workforce analysis and reporting for Department of Defense (DoD) and external government agencies, support for health insurance programs, managing benefits, and reporting certification and training. DCPDS supports the entire civilian HR life cycle, with transactions and information that reflect acquiring, assigning, training and development, sustaining and managing HR compensation, managing organizations, supporting benefits management, and separation or termination of civilian personnel. This investment directly supports the strategic goals of the DoD HR Strategic Plan, developing and implementing innovative HR management solutions that enable the DCPDS customer ?leaders, managers, and employees throughout the Department ? to ensure the DoD civilian work force is able to effectively support the Warfighter and the national security mission.

DCRM utilizes an online Customer Information Control System (CICS) application that uses data in Virtual Storage Access Method (VSAM) files and a multi-file (flat file) structure. The system uses a Job Control Language (JCL) based operating environment to process the COBOL II and SAS based software applications. It uses an IBM z/OS mainframe operating system and is accessible through the web, via the DISA hosted Multi Host Internet Access Portal (MIAP). investmentDescription: Educates future commanders, battle staffs, and soldiers to exploit the new digital capabilities on the battlefield.  The ABCS is the principle digital command and control system of systems for battlefield commanders from battalion to corps. ABCS builds the Common Tactical Picture (CTP) depicting the complete tactical battle space picture control measures and friendly and enemy platforms near real time.  ABCS consists of Global Command and Control System - Army (GCCS-A), Advanced Field Artillery Tactical Data System (AFATDS), All Source Analysis System (ASAS), Battle Command Sustainment Support System  (BCS3), Army Missile Defense Warning System (AMDWS), Maneuver Control System (MCS), Force XXI Battle Command Battalion/Brigade and Below (FBCB2), and Tactical Airspace Information System (TAIS). The institutional training base capability enables the schools and training centers to create a networked ABCS learning environment to transition soldiers from analog to digital thinking and warfighting.  The Secure Distributed Digital Training System (SD2TS) capability is required by TRADOC schools and training centers to leverage institutional training into the operational domain thus facilitating the transition of soldiers from analog to digital thinking and warfighting.  Project requirements include training system architecture and the technologies to conduct automated institutional training via a virtual, online, integrated system of audio/visual, and learning management and control tools capable of supporting both standard Windows-based applications and Sun/Solaris-based ABCS applications.

It is a key enabler of the Standardized Tactical Entry Point (STEP) and Department of Defense Teleport programs, which provide deployed Warfighters with global connectivity to military command and control systems, reach back to the sustaining base, and access to enterprise information resources and the Defense Information Systems Network. The DCSS also interfaces with the national strategic communications infrastructure to support Presidential and senior DoD leadership communications. The system includes both manual and automated patching facilities to ensure flexible and efficient utilization of both ground equipment and satellite resources and quick restoral of critical communications circuits during unexpected outages.

investmentDescription: A Zero Trust (ZT) model assumes that breaches occur and verifies each request as though it originates from an open network. Regardless of where the request originates or what resource it accesses, ZT teaches us to "never trust, always verify." Every access request is fully authenticated, authorized, and encrypted before granting access. Comprehensive analytics and intelligence are utilized to detect and respond to anomalies in real time. DOI developed a ZT Strategy Implementation Plan in response to OMB directive M-22-09; Moving the U.S. Government Toward Zero Trust (ZT) Cybersecurity Principles. In FY 2022, the OCIO along with bureaus and offices, refined initial cost estimates, defined metrics for measuring progress against the DOI Zero Trust Strategy, and developed Zero Trust technical standards. During FY 23-24 OCIO is developing the foundation for an advanced stage of ZT implementation for FY25 and a goal of an optimal stage of maturity by FY30. Investment initiation: 2022.

investmentDescription: The Reliability Asset Monitoring (RAM) system provides Warner Robins Air Logistics Center (WR-ALC), Ogden Air Logistics Center (OO-ALC), and Eglin Air Force Base the means for assessing present performance levels as well as predicting future reliability standards for current Air Force missile and Precision Guided Munitions (PGM) All-Up-Round (AUR) assets, unassembled components, and subcomponents, as well as specific Navy assets. The RAM system receives and maintains, based upon each missile/munitions program offices' needs, the as built data of each asset, the field level activity data (including TCTO compliances, reconfigurations, flight hours, testing data, and location change (shipment & receipt) data and the depot repair data. The RAM System tracks the munitions performance down to the lowest serialized components and maintains the history of each asset from cradle to grave. Tactical Munitions Reporting System (TMRS) is a field reporting program, specified in AFI 21-201, that provides the munitions shops the status of their PGM AUR and unassembled component (including serviceability, configuration, periodic inspections and TCTOs) and maintains the required munitions historical data for their assets (AFTO Form 95 and 244 records). The field munitions organizations are required by Technical Order (T.O.) 21M-1-101 to report specific reliability and logistic data to the RAM Program Office. TMRS has automated the data collection specified in AFI 21-201 and T.O. 21M-1-101 and creates the required AFTO Form data for submission to the RAM Program Office. TMRS data is submitted through both email and web input. As new munitions programs test sets develop the capability to download the test set logistics data, TMRS reads and processes those logistic files, eliminating the need for the field TMRS personnel from manually updating each munitions asset tested. TMRS also provides for T. O. 11A-1-1 (Conventional Munitions Restrictions and Suspensions) identification and suspension of munitions assets, down to the serial numbers of components embedded within a built up AUR. There is no other system that provides this data. TMRS allows the field units to create shipping files containing all current and historical data for the munitions that are being shipped; the receiving unit then has automated data available in TMRS to give them the status of the assets received. This system does not meet the criteria for Internal Use Software (IUS) reporting.

investmentDescription: Protective DNS protects agencies against malicious internet destinations, making the network inherently more secure. Protective DNS intercepts and filters all DNS requests made by network devices. When users enter a URL or follow a link from source such as email, embedded link in a document, or link from a website, Protective DNS intercepts this request and checks the URL against a list of suspicious or known malicious domain names and IP addresses. If the domain or IP is on the suspicious or known malicious list, Protective DNS blocks the outbound request. investmentDescription: Navy Cash is an evolution of the Automated Teller Machines-At-Sea (ATMs-At-Sea) program which began installing ATMs on board ships in 1988. Navy Cash program is partnership between the US Navy and the US Treasury. Navy Cash replaced the cash-based economy on board ship with a stored-value-card, electronic-funds-transfer system in 2001. Navy Cash combines stored value chip technology and a magnetic strip to virtually eliminate the need for Sailors and Marines to carry cash. On the ship, a chip based, secure, electronic purse provides for a cashless environment and provides cardholders with electronic access to their personal funds in checking and savings accounts ashore. Off the ship, the magnetic strip on the back of the card provides a branded pre-paid debit feature for access to the funds in Navy Cash accounts and can be used at more than 23 million MasterCard? acceptance locations and more than 1 million ATMs in over 210 countries and territories worldwide.

investmentDescription: The ASC Enterprise Board (E-Board) provides the ASC, AFSB Commanders and staff mission critical information needed to identify potential problem areas, systemic issues within the command, trends across sites and/or mission areas, opportunities to apply continuous improvement techniques, opportunities to replicate best practices and standardize processes where possible, and metrics for tracking and analyzing process improvements. This status is available for individual End Items and grouped upwards to many levels such as End Items by Home Base, Major Command (MAJCOM) and Program. The system provides manager dashboard at all levels with graphical representation of the End Item Status for all levels of production status meetings. These status meetings are held when anyone up and down the management chain needs production status. Using graphical tools, it allows the particular end user capabilities to drill down from higher level status charts to individual operations on the End Item along with particular mechanics time and individual status. The system provides metrics to all levels of production managers including resource. The LEAD ASRS has been storing and retrieving parts at LEAD for over 15 years.  The loss of LEAD ASRS would negatively impact LEAD?s ability to meet production schedules and be competitive in today?s manufacturing environment.  LEAD ASRS also utilizes conventional storage areas to handle oversized items.  The LEAD ASRS is able to store a large volume of parts in a relatively small footprint that gives improved visibility and control of repair parts needed for the refurbishment of army assets at LEAD. investmentDescription: The Department of Defense Electronic Official Personnel Folder (DoD eOPF) initiative directly supports the management of Human Resources (HR) records for civilian employees in accordance with the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Guide to Personnel Recordkeeping (GPR). The eOPF is an OPM HR technology service mandated by the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) for all Executive Branch agencies to eliminate paper Official Personnel Folders (OPFs) by December 2013. The OPM business case aligns eOPF under the HR Line of Business sub-functions: HR Management, Benefits Management, Personnel Management, Information & Technology Management, and Records Retention. The documents in employee OPFs are essential to HR business operations such as merit promotion, non-competitive placements, position management, and retirement, benefits and entitlements processing. Today, a hardcopy OPF can only be accessed by one person at a time and is often not locally available. These limitations impact processing time and HR operations efficiency. Through on-demand Web-based access to personnel folders, eOPF enables 24/7 concurrent direct access to personnel information by HR staffs, managers, and employees from any authorized location. All of the records associated with Federal employment history, benefits, and entitlements are collected and maintained in the eOPF. Some of these records are auto-populated through an interface with the Defense Civilian Personnel Data System (DCPDS). The eOPF allows HR staffs to electronically transfer personnel records from one agency to another when employees move between agencies.  In addition, eOPF records for separating employees can be electronically transferred to the National Personnel Records Center (NPRC) for preservation. These attributes of eOPF will improve the efficiency of HR operations. In addition, the enhanced records access and transfer feature in eOPF, will eliminate the time and cost of shipping hardcopy OPFs between locations. The eOPF also supports the elimination of the resources such as equipment and facilities associated with maintaining paper records. The Defense Civilian Personnel Advisory Service is centrally funding DoD eOPF implementation and sustainment with the DoD Components are funding eOPF back-file conversion and day-forward document scanning. The majority of the other Federal agencies are already benefiting from the use of eOPF. The efficiencies to be derived make eOPF an essential investment for the DoD.

There will also be portable and vehicle mountable versions of the same hardware and software that will be used to meet shorter term requirements at bases throughout the MAJCOM. Manpower Query System provides queries of TFMMS billet, end strength & activity data. N10 Executive Dashboard provides key financial metrics & status of key program management & audit readiness efforts. Navy Econometric Model estimates officer & enlisted recruiting & retention parameters & effect of assignment incentives. Navy Subspecialist System validates subspecialty-coded billets, prioritizes & removes excess authorizations to ensure supply meets demand for highest priority billets. Navy Total Force Strength Model produces timely & accurate Navy Active Enlisted & Full-Time Support strength projections. New Accession Training provides active & reserve pay & personnel data to satisfy requirements of Financial Improvement Audit Readiness. Permanent Change of Station Model evaluates cost & effect of execution alternatives & provides measures for decision-makers creating execution plan. Selective Reenlistment Bonus Model supports budget formulation/justification & more efficient allocation of resources across targeted critical skill sets. Web Full Time Support Navy Officer Personnel Planning System reconciles annual & FYDP plans with actuals to generate budget submissions. Web NOPPS captures official active component officer end strength activity based on OPINS transactions in aggregate & community level detail for certifying congressional compliance, budgeting, reporting & creating the FYDP. investmentDescription: The Naval Center for Cost Analysis (NCCA) is responsible for both the Naval VAMOSC System and the NCCAWeb System, hereafter referred to as the Naval VAMOSC Application System.  NCCA?s organizational mission is also to guide, direct and strengthen cost analysis within the Department of the Navy; to ensure the preparation of credible cost estimates of the resources required to develop, procure and operate military systems and forces in support of planning, programming, budgeting and acquisition management; and to perform such other functions and tasks as may be directed by higher authority. The Naval VAMOSC Application System supports this mission by providing cost and non-cost data collection and reporting of US Navy and US Marine Corps historical weapon system operating and support (O&S) costs.OSD PA&E provides executive oversight for the Services' VAMOSC programs.  Naval VAMOSC Applictation System collects and reports the historical operating and support costs of Navy and Marine Corps weapon systems and personnel.  Data is collected from over 130 unique sources that contains over 1200 unique data elements.  Some of the raw data is collected from these sources in an automated approach, while others are files provided manually by individual program offices.  Business intelligence software provides the user interface.  Registered DoD users may access the data from the websites using a browser.  Funding provides for source data collection, updating of internal dictionary tables, database operations and maintenance, data quality assurance, system administration, user documentation, user conference logistics, training, special analyses, website support, user account maintenance, and user support.  Funding also pays for the operations and support of the Operating and Support Costs Analysis Model that is populated with VAMOSC data.  Many of these tasks are currently outsourced.  Although the Naval VAMOSC Application System is in maintenance mode for many of the ongoing systems, enhancements are continuously being evaluated to make the system more manageable and applicable to the user environment.  Enhancements have typically been limited to the inclusion of additional data elements (e.g., food costs on ships) collected from VAMOSC sources as they became available, but also entirely new data sets are being added to the database as new information is uncovered.

investmentDescription: Calibration Sets ? Connected (CALSETS-C) is a variant Calibration Set 2000 that provides the system the capability of a connection to the Non-secure Internet Protocol Router Network (NIPRNET).  It is a suite of components, including software (SW) and hardware, primarily of Non Developmental Items (NDI)/Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) equipment, which is used by U.S. Army calibrators to calibrate General Purpose (GP) and selected Special Purpose (SP) Test, Measurement, and Diagnostic Equipment (TMDE) in the tactical and civilian calibration laboratories of the U.S. Army.    The CALSETS-C calibration labs are designated as follows:  AN/GSM-286, AN/GSM-287, AN/GSM-421, AN/GSM-705, and Reference.  The CALSETS-C includes four-laptop type Instrument Controllers (IC) allowing for concurrent calibration and repair operations.  CALSETS-C is used as a force multiplier in the U.S. Army Calibration laboratories. CALSETS-C is a unique maintenance information system used by the U.S. Army Calibrators to perform their mission in a more efficient way.   At present, the bulk of the workload is done in a Government Off the Shelf (GOTS) run-time environment (RTE), which is built on an opened system model.  This GOTS RTE is a force multiplier.  The calibrator enters a model number, and the GOTS RTE displays the corresponding procedure.  The procedure contains the standards needed, found in the Calibration Laboratories, and the operational steps to connect and perform the calibration/repair.  The standards are varied (such as scopes, & calibrators) and in the hundreds.  They are scheduled to be replace/upgraded at a level of 10%/year under the approval of Army G3 and funding availability. CALSETS-C does not communicate with other U.S. Army systems. The calibrators use the NIPRNET to keep CALSETS-C at a harden level by manually downloading SW patches to address vulnerabilities and TMDE programs needed to calibrate and repair GP and Selected SP TMDEs found in the U.S. Army TB 43-180.

investmentDescription: Within the Department of the Navy (DON), Secretary of the Navy Instruction (4855.3) establishes the requirements for all DON Activities to utilize the Product Data Reporting and Evaluation Program (PDREP) Automated Information System (AIS) for processing supplier performance information. This SECNAV Instruction establishes PDREP-AIS as the DON single source to support mandatory reporting, collection, sharing, retrieval and analysis of supplier performance information identified in the Code of Federal Regulations (CFR), Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR), the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS), the Navy Marine Corps Acquisition Regulation Supplement (NMCARS) and other DOD/DON regulations. PDREP-AIS is the DON authoritative source for Critical Safety Items (CSI) and Counterfeit Material Reporting.  PDREP is the DOD authoritative source for collection of supplier warranty information.  The PDREP AIS also supports the DON requirement to provide supplier performance information to the DoD Past Performance Information Retrieval System (PPIRS) for use by all DOD. PDREP provides critical supplier performance information to DON components and Program Executive Offices (PEOs) and works across DOD component lines to collect and share this critical information. The PDREP-AIS is Item Unique Identification (IUID) compliant providing automated data retrieval from the IUID registry for easier reporting of Unique Item Identifier (UII) materials.  PDREP has been identified at a DON-IT KM/CM Program of Record. investmentDescription: Secret Internet Protocol Router Network (SIPRNET) In-Transit Visibility (S-ITV) is a web based capability that provides the same information to its users as the Radio Frequency In-transit Visibility (RF-ITV) system.  RF-ITV is in the Business Mission Area (BMA) Logistics domain, Army Information Technology Registry (AITR) number DA05708.  A Defense Information System Agency (DISA) Cross Domain Enterprise Solution (CDES) is used to move all RF-ITV data from the low side to the high side.  This allows users that are working in the S-ITV system and in a classified environment to access in-transit visibility (ITV) data without having to move to the low side to obtain shipment statues.  Through the RF-ITV system, S-ITV receives Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) data from active RFID tags, fixed/handheld interrogators, and Satellite Tracking Systems (STS).  These devices support the dissemination of In-Transit Visibility (ITV) information required by the Department of Defense (DoD), Coalition Partners, and Allies of the United States. By using RFID tags and STS devices on shipments of supplies equipment, the S-ITV system traces the identity, status, and location of cargo from origin (depot or vendor) to destination.  The data from these two technologies is combined, processed, and accessed via web-based maps and reports to provide global logistics support to the Joint Force. The multi-tiered RFID/STS architecture extends to over 41 countries where location visibility information is collected, centralized, and distributed to selected DOD logistics systems through standard Service Oriented Architecture (SOA) based Extensible Markup Language (XML) web services and point-to-point interfaces.  All inbound data provided to the S-ITV system comes from the RF-ITV system.  The S-ITV outbound data exchanges are to the Central Command (CENTCOM) Logistics Common Operating Picture (LogCOP) and Global Combat Support System - Joint (GCSS-J) systems.

investmentDescription: PDM has three major uses: (1) Configuration Management, (2) Technical  Drawing Repository/Data Management, and (3) Workflow. The on-line technical drawing repository provides users the capability to view approved drawings utilizing free viewers. A drawing report includes the ability to view the latest revision of the drawing, as well as any previous revisions that are loaded in the system. The report details all outstanding changes not yet incorporated, all incorporated changes, any withdrawn, deferred, or disapproved changes written against the drawing, and any identified red flags, RFRs, or DMS cases pending against the drawing. The workflow module of PDM facilitates the routing for review all items created on the system, as well as any other items (e.g. plans, CDRLs, status reports, etc) by allowing the user the ability to attach files. The workflow module includes on-line comment creation and resolution. The system also gives the user the capability to tie or link related items on the system to each other.
