investmentDescription: The US Army Unemployment Compensation for Ex-Service Members (UCX) application determines eligibility of individuals to receive unemployment compensation funded by the US Army. Using information obtained from an Ex-Service member's Department of Defense (DD) Form 214 as received through the Transition Processing module of Installation Support Modules (ISM), UCX determines if a separated Soldier is eligible for unemployment compensation.  Claimant names and Social Security Numbers are provided by the 54 states and territories of the United States.  Most claims are received electronically from the Federal Claims Control Center (FCCC) web site, while the US Virgin Islands still submits claims through the US Postal Service.  Records for eligible individuals are passed to the archive with no further action required.  An exception occurs when an individual was retired from the Army; where a letter is generated to inform the applicable state of the individual's retirement income.  Currently, retirement information is done separately and manually inputted into the record.  In the future, UCX will link with the Defense Retiree and Annuitant Pay System (DRAS) for retiree pensions, the Interactive Personnel Electronic Records Management System (iPERMS), ISM for DD Form 214 access, and the Defense Enrollment Eligibility Reporting System (DEERS).  If the individual is ineligible the record is flagged to have it reviewed by an analyst to determine eligibility.  If the claimant is confirmed as ineligible, a letter of ineligibility will be generated.  These letters are presently sent via USPS, but will be sent via electronic data transfer in the future.

CFIUS Case Management System.

The Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States (CFIUS) was established in 1975 under Executive Order 11858 to monitor the impact of foreign investment in the United States, and to coordinate and implement federal policy on such investment. CFIUS is composed of nine voting member agencies. The Committee’s unique design leverages the skills, subject matter expertise, and integrated analysis of Committee members and other relevant agencies. CFIUS voting members include:
* Department of the Treasury
* Department of Commerce
* Department of Defense
* Department of Energy
* Department of Homeland Security
* Department of Justice
* Department of State
* Office of Science Technology and Policy
* Office of the United States Trade Representative

As both Chair and member of CFIUS, Treasury is responsible for leading CFIUS in establishing policies, implementing processes and functions, and managing its daily operations. Treasury participates in every aspect of CFIUS, including reviews and investigations, policy and international relations, mitigation monitoring and enforcement, non-notified transaction analysis, legal support, and national security threat assessments. The Office of International Affairs (IA) is responsible for case management and coordination and representing the Committee to parties that file notices or declarations. The Office of General Counsel (OGC) provides legal support to IA and is responsible for certain analyses conducted on each notice filed with CFIUS.

The Foreign Investment Risk Review Modernization Act of 2018 (FIRRMA) strengthened CFIUS to better address national security concerns arising from some types of investments and transactions that were previously outside its jurisdiction. Additionally, FIRRMA modernized Committee processes to better enable timely and effective reviews of covered transactions. FIRRMA also established the CFIUS Fund (the Fund), to be administered by the chairperson (the Secretary of the Treasury), to accept appropriated funds for these expanded responsibilities and functions, and to collect filing fees.

investmentDescription: This system is a component of the overall Air and Missile Defense (AMD) architecture and will provide for an incrementally fielded Integrated Air and Missile Defense Fire Control System/capability for the composite Army Air and Missile Defense Brigades. The Sentinel system is used with the Forward Area Air Defense Command and Control (FAAD C2) element and is a key component to the Integrated Air and Missile Defense (IAMD) architecture via the IAMD Battle Command System (IBCS) to provide critical air surveillance of the forward areas.  The Sentinel currently consists of two primary variants: the enhanced radar variant AN/MPQ-64A3 system mounted on a High Mobility Multi-purpose Wheeled Vehicle (HMMWV) and the AN/MPQ-64A3 mounted on a 2.5 ton trailer and towed by an armored Family of Medium Tactical Vehicle (FMTV) platform to meet force protection and Integrated Air and Missile Defense Battle Command System (IBCS) system requirements. The fielding of the FMTV configuration AN/MPQ-64A3 assets will be complete in FY 2019. Sentinel also consists of Identification Friend or Foe (IFF), and Forward Area Air Defense (FAAD) Command, Control and Intelligence (C2I) interfaces. The radar is deployed in both an air defense role and a force protection role for Counter-Rocket, Artillery, and Mortar (C-RAM) missions. The sensor is an advanced three-dimensional battlefield X-Band air defense phased-array radar with an instrumented range of 75 kilometers. Sentinel is capable of operating day or night, in adverse weather conditions, in the battlefield environments of dust, smoke, aerosols and enemy countermeasures. It provides 360-degree azimuth coverage for acquisition tracking. Sentinel contributes to the digital battlefield by automatically detecting, classifying, identifying and reporting targets (cruise missiles, unmanned aerial systems, rotary wing and fixed wing aircraft). Sentinel acquires targets sufficiently forward of the battle area to allow weapons reaction time and engagement at optimum ranges. Sentinel's integrated IFF reduces the potential for fratricide of US and Coalition aircraft.

investmentDescription: The intent/purpose of the SCS program is to support worldwide Air Force readiness and sustainability to the warfighter by providing faster, more accurate allocation and movement decisions regarding Air Force material. The SCS operational mission is to manage depot-level supply activities and provide enhanced processing of stock control transactions and management information at United States Air Force (USAF) and United States Marine Corp (USMC) inventory control points. SCS's primary asset management functions are to provide current asset visibility, maintain balances, process requisitions, and provide status to worldwide customers. The high-level asset management functional areas contained in SCS are requisitioning, item management data, inventory, due-in/receipts, materiel returns (excess), controlled issue of items, depot support, miscellaneous supporting functions, and reutilization and dispositioning. SCS is an on-line and real-time data system that is in a steady state life cycle phase. SCS has implemented Graphical User Interface (GUI) Windows-type screens, is web enabled, is web accessible via the AF Portal, and has separated business applications from data. The current SCS is composed of both the following modernized and un-modernized subsystems: Item Manager Wholesale Requisition Process (IMWRP), Wholesale Management and Efficiency Reports (WMER), Inventory Storage (INSTOR), Reportable Asset Management Process (RAMP), Special Support Stock Control (SSSC), Readiness Based Leveling (RBL), Redistribution and Disposition System (RDS) (formerly, the D067 legacy system), Financial Inventory Accounting and Billing System (FIABS), Wholesale and Retail Receiving and Shipping (WARRS), and Shipping Information System (SIS).

investmentDescription: The Army Accessions Enterprise (AAE) is data-driven, analytics-enabled, Soldier workforce-centric, and customer-focused. It provides the Army?s strength through its four (4) missions: (1) enlist Soldiers, (2) commission Officers, (3) fulfill In-Service requirements, and (4) support and sustain. The enterprise serves the Army well, but requires modernization to meet emerging requirements and ensure continued success.  The Accessions Information Environment (AIE) is a program of record established to confront the challenges facing the AAE. AIE will implement new business practices and modern technology. It will be a fully integrated enterprise level capability enabling transparency, efficiency and effectiveness of the accessions workforce to acquire best-qualified talent to meet all Army manning requirements.  AIE has not been designated a National Security System (NSS). Data and analytics drive the AAE. Therefore, the AIE will be built on a foundation of data, information technology architectures and standards, infrastructure, and analytical tools to achieve a modern end-state using configurable, commercial off the shelf (COTS) software. The envisioned end-state is a net-centric enterprise solution characterized by standardized architecture and data formats; maximized authoritative data discovery and sharing; fully integrated capabilities; intuitive ability to access, visualize, assess, and understand data; integrated and automated business processes; and single source data entry. Primary AIE users are Army Recruiting Command (USAREC), U.S. Army Cadet Command (USACC), and U.S, Army National Guard (ARNG), with a total of 28,200 core end users. AIE will operationalize eight (8) accessions enterprise core capabilities: Lead Generation/Management, Prospecting, Interviewing, Processing, Marketing, Intelligence, Training/Leader Development, and Pay and Incentives. The following system objectives have been established:  Secure, Interoperable Solution; Mobility; Connectivity; Data Access, Accuracy, and Timeliness; Device-agnostic, Real-time Access from Multiple Domains; Interface to Systems of Record; Common Operating Picture; Knowledge Management; Leadership End-to-end Enterprise Visibility; Single Source Record, and Automated Business Processes.  The AIE target infrastructure is a commercial cloud hosted on a commercial network.

partOfITPortfolio: Part 2. IT Investments for Mission Support Services
investmentTitle: DEFENSE CIVILIAN HUMAN RESOURCES MANAGEMENT SYSTEM
investmentDescription: The Defense Civilian Human Resources Management System (DCHRMS) will be the Department's enterprise civilian Human Resources (HR) automated transactional system that supports one-third of the federal work force. Network operations span worldwide and are online 24/7. DCHRMS is being configured to support the entire civilian HR life cycle, with transactions and information that reflect acquiring, assigning, training and development, sustaining and managing HR compensation, managing organizations, supporting benefits management, and separation or termination of civilian personnel. Reporting will include leadership-level corporate reporting across the enterprise, as well as individual Military Department and Defense Agency customer information. DCHRMS is the product of the migration of capability from the Defense Civilian Personnel Data System (DCPDS) on a Federalized version of Oracle's E-Business Suite ERP, to Oracle's Fusion Software as a Service (SaaS)  environment in compliance with the Data Center Optimization Initiative (DCOI) an in compliance with the May 2018 Reform Management Group approved strategy to replace DCPDS with a Software as a Service solution. DCHRMS will consolidate disparate databases into one; establish a single employee record for each member and exploit efficiencies gained through the use of the systems' additional offerings, such as performance management. DCHRMS will implement capability incrementally by populations. DCPDS will continue to support populations not yet migrated to DCHRMS until full deployment of DCHRMS, until final decommissioning can occur. This investment directly supports the strategic goals of the DoD HR Strategic Plan, developing and implementing innovative HR management solutions that enable the customer -leaders, managers, and employees throughout the Department - to ensure the DoD civilian work force is able to effectively support the Warfighter and the national security mission.

RF-ITV uses Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) devices to support the dissemination of ITV information required by the Department of Defense (DoD), Coalition Partners, and Allies of the United States. By using RFID tags on shipments of supplies equipment, the RF-ITV system traces the identity, status, and location of cargo from origin (depot or vendor) to destination. It also receives near real-time position reports for conveyances equipped with various Satellite Tracking Systems (STS). Data from these two technologies is combined, processed, and accessed via web-based maps and reports, and provides global logistics support to the Joint Force. The RF-ITV Infrastructure includes over 1,700 nodal read and write sites located in 37 countries worldwide. These nodes are placed at strategic choke points throughout the Defense Transportation System (DTS) (i.e., all Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) depots and strategic aerial ports and seaports). RF-ITV is a DoD approved infrastructure that provides in-transit visibility beyond the Theater Distribution Center (TDC).

investmentTitle: Interactive Personnel Electronic Records Management System
investmentDescription: Interactive Personnel Electronic Records Management System (iPERMS) is a highly net-centric system established to provide electronic document management of the Army Military Human Resource Record (AMHRR) which contains the Official Military Personnel File (OMPF), and to support life-cycle management of Soldiers. iPERMS operates on the Non-classified Internet Protocol Router Network (NIPRNet) and provides records management in war, mobilization and peace as required by 10 USC and 44 USC. It is the system of record and storage for the AMHRR which contains various document disposition schedules including pay substantiating documentation during a Soldier?s service. iPERMS is the Army?s authorized repository for the AMHRR, and is the historical and authoritative source to authenticate benefits, entitlements and service. The OMPF is the permanent chronological account of a Soldier?s career from accession to the Army through separation, and is an accumulative account of information maintained as evidence of events and decisions during the course of the Soldier?s service. iPERMS maintains and safeguards the OMPF for 62 years after separation which then transfers to the National Archives for storage as a public record. It is a secure system accessed through a restricted portal requiring authorization for level of access. It enhances record quality, optimizes storage and retrieval, reduces operating costs, improves selection board support, and provides numerous other non-quantitative benefits. iPERMS actively supports DoD strategies for use of net-centric automated information systems by providing a method of maintaining the AMHRR for Soldiers in the Active Army, Army Reserve, and Army National Guard. iPERMS complies with conventions instituted by the Defense Personnel Record Imaging System (DPRIS), established as a Joint committee to ensure consistency between DoD components and provide a migration path for imaging systems. Soldiers, commanders, career managers at all levels, human resource managers, selection boards, and other authorized officials can access iPERMS at all times in a secure mode worldwide. Veterans and Federal agencies such as the Department of Veteran Affairs, the Office of Personnel Management, the Department of Labor, the National Archives and Records Administration, and other non-DA agencies with appropriate access credentials, may access AMHRR documents/records from DPRIS which retrieves the requested document(s) through a portal with iPERMS.

The purpose of AMCATS is to account for all munitions and explosives received on Redstone Arsenal and White Sands Missile Range from the time the material arrives, to its ultimate use, shipment off-post, or destruction.  AMCATS automates customer requisitioning of munitions and explosives in support of training conducted by the United States Army Ordinance Munitions and Electronic Maintenance School (OMEMS) and research and development activities conducted by the Redstone Technical Test Center (RTTC) and the Aviation and Missile Command Research, Development and Engineering Center (AMRDEC).  AMCATS is designed primarily to support the research and development activities distinct to the Army Test and Evaluation Command (ATEC). It also supports the training of the Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) Warfighter, and the Federal Bureau of Investigations, through OMEMS, trains Bomb Disposal Squads for police departments from all over the country. AMCATS is now capable of reporting on-hand balances of training assets and Category I missiles and rockets to the Army Support Command and to Joint Munitions Command on a daily basis. The people who benefit from the use of AMCATS are the Research and Development engineers and test personnel who depend on the installation ammunition supply point (ASP) to initially receive the munitions and then provide the munitions to the engineers and testers who ultimately test and improve munitions that support the Warfighter - specifically RTTC, AMRDEC, and White Sands Missile Range in their live fire testing efforts.  AMCATS provides real-time processing and does not interface with any other products.

investmentDescription: The Defense Corporate Database/Warehouse (DCD/DCW) serves as the DFAS shared data environment to interface, standardize, and share data between financial management systems. The DCW is a static data source that supports reporting, audit, and analysis. It provides central data warehouse capability to store, query, and report DoD financial data. The DCW provides customers access to their financial information through data marts where it can be used for evaluation, conducting trend analyses, decision-making, and auditing. Added function provides an integrated environment for reporting Cost of War (COW), Disaster Relief (DR), and other contingency efforts. Services and Defense Agencies have one consolidated location to view and analyze all data for reporting purposes. DCD/DCW also supports the following modules: Departmental Reporting for Other Defense Organizations (ODO), Metrics and Initiatives Office (M&IO), and Performance Measures Indicators System (PMIS).  DCD/DCW supports data transfers from the DFAS Indianapolis, Departmental Reporting for Other Defense Organizations (ODO) to support critical path, monthly and year-end financial reporting for Other Defense Organizations.  Metrics and Initiatives Office (M&IO) is the single data collection hub for the Agency Metrics Reporting Program. investmentTitle: DUGWAY PROVING GROUND KEY MANAGEMENT SYSTEM
investmentDescription: The KeyTrax Automated Key Management System maintains positive control over keys to US Army buildings on Dugway Proving Ground. The system integrates several technologies to automatically identify users (key custodians and key recipients), read key numbers, and record transaction details. It also enforces certain security criteria to ensure that only properly authorized individuals are able to draw the keys to any particular building. In summary, Key Control automates all verification and data collection activities associated with each key issue and receipt transaction. The Key Control system includes hardware devices integrated with a custom software application. Personnel can login using a fingerprint reader. The system identifies precisely which key(s) an individual is checking in or out by reading a passive Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) device attached to each key. It then verifies that the individual can sign out that key. Using relationships and restrictions stored in its database, Key trax identifies the building to which each scanned key belongs, and checks to ensure that the recipient only receives keys to buildings for which he or she has authorized access. Several categories of authorization are supported, including security classification, storage category, owning activity, and special access limitations. All relevant conditions must be met before the system will process the transaction. Key Control includes a number of standard reports designed to support various user requirements:   ?	All keys currently outstanding ?	All keys issued to a particular user ?	All buildings in which material has been moved for a particular date ?	All key issue transactions for a given date ?	All key issue/receipt transactions for a specified building over a specified time period ?	All key inventory stored in the Key Control database.

investmentDescription: The LMP is a System that builds, sustains, and generates warfighting capabilities using one of the largest, fully-integrated supply chain and maintenance, repair, and overhaul solutions in the world. It is an SAP-based commercial-off-the-shelf Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) solution that manages and tracks orders and delivery of materiel, supports the Army Materiel Command industrial base for repair and overhaul of Army equipment, and serves as the General Ledger for the Army Working Capital Fund. The LMP meets the Army IT logistics vision of a long-overdue transformation from legacy national applications to a modernized logistics enterprise solution across AMC to arsenals, depots, other non-depot maintenance activities at the National level, and the Defense Finance Accounting Service (DFAS). In 2014, the U.S. Special Operations Command (USSOCOM) also began using the LMP system.  The LMP support is critical to the Army achieving an integrated enterprise solution that enables materiel readiness and provides asset management and accountability, architecture and acquisition compliancy, and financial transparency.  The LMP handles more than 7M transactions daily and manages approximately $16B in AWCF inventory. It is deployed to approximately 23,000 users in more than 50 Army and DoD locations, and 56 trading partners with nearly 300 unique interfaces, including interfaces with other Army ERP systems - Army Enterprise Systems Integration Program (AESIP), Global Combat Support System-Army (GCSS-Army), and General Fund Enterprise Business System (GFEBS).     The Army implemented the baseline system through three deployments between 2003 and 2010. The Acquisition Decision Memorandum (ADM) dated 27 December 2011 placed the LMP deployed /operational production baseline (i.e. Increment 1) in the sustainment phase of the acquisition lifecycle. This information is then used to organize and prepare flight (including cargo airdrop) and weapons delivery planning data (e.g., maps, charts, imagery, flight logs, radar predications, and navigation databases) that is electronically transferred to aircraft and weapons. It helps to increase wartime sortie rates while improving aircrew and aircraft survivability and aircrew readiness. This MPS procurement effort takes advantage of the rapid increase in PC-based technology to enable high-end computing on increasingly smaller and more mission-oriented devices.  The various programs procure UNIX and PC-based mission planning computers, which provide a flexible, configurable, and cost effective solution for increasing tactical and strategic capabilities to meet the continuum of operations ranging from peacetime contingencies to conventional and nuclear wartime mission planning requirements.  Each program has shifted its hardware emphasis from a small number of large, complex planning systems to a larger number of smaller, more personal, planning devices tailored to user needs.  This adjustment was made for the following technology-driven reasons:  the evolutionary nature of mission planning requires hardware changes to meet overall system requirements; advances in commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) technology make available new capabilities which may lower component costs or address component obsolescence; and changes in number, type, and deployment of aircraft/weapons require changes in the number of UNIX and PC-based mission planning computers and their concept of operation.

The NSIPS environment also provides special application modules for stake holder communities such as the processing of officer acceptance and oath of office when they are commissioned, career information management for career counselors, Navy retention data for manpower planners, permanent change of station travel funds obligations and expenditures for travel planners, healthcare professional incentives authorizations and tracking, and SEAL/SWCC special qualifications tracking and management. investmentDescription: AFITEDU is the Air Force Institute of Technology (AFIT) educational IT network, providing infrastructure, hardware and essential management tools required to provide information technology core services to approximately 1800 students, faculty, staff and over 15,000 distance learning students world-wide. This unique network must support administration, unique instructional and academic management services, and support state-of-the-art research in engineering and science.  AFITEDU provides for the information technology network infrastructure to meet Institute-wide requirements for AFIT's unique education, research, consulting, and academic support missions.  Aside from its fundamental role in providing advanced academic education (masters and PhDs) for USAF, DoD, and foreign military officers, AFIT also makes significant contributions to the development of modern and future Air Force cyberspace weapon systems.  This program allows for the acquisition of integrated networking technology solutions and leading-edge infrastructure components that will keep AFIT at the forefront of technology.  These investments include data and application servers; enterprise backup and storage systems; high-speed, parallel computing devices; high bandwidth internetworking equipment to support extensive IT research; and all associated software.  This integrated IT infrastructure provides a high capacity academic computing network supporting all AFIT students, faculty, and staff applications, with the exception of specialized laboratory processing applications that require very large computing power satisfied only by supercomputer class machines.  Finally, this program enables AFIT to continue its graduate and continuing education, research, and consulting mission without being dependent on outside organizations for IT support.  This is a critical factor in maintaining AFIT's academic accreditation via the North Central Association of Colleges and Schools and with the Accreditation Board for Engineering Technology (ABET).

investmentDescription: The RSRS system components are installed on Windows based platforms and hosted within the trusted enclave and NIPRNET Public Access Zone inside the SPAWAR Systems Center Atlantic, New Orleans (SSCLANT NOLA) Extended Demilitarized Zone (EDMZ). The RSRS architecture is an industry standard, n-tier implementation operating on Commercial-off-the-Shelf (COTS) hardware and software. The RSRS system uses an Oracle 11 Relational Database Management System (RDMS) for data storage. The BMC Distributed Server Option (DSO) provides enterprise wide synchronization of the SPAWARSYSCOM regional sites and local servers. Access to the RSRS system is available through web interface. Data transmissions are protected by the use of secure ports, protocols and network services. The SSCLANT network provides a secure environment with common services and resources available to support connectivity between hosted systems applications and the affiliated system interfaces with user population, The RSRS system interfaces are described in Section 9.0 of this CAP. Firewall, data encryption and intrusion detection services are implemented as part of the SSC LANT enterprise network architecture. The RSRS system provides an integrated architecture for problem resolution and tracking for the SSC NOLA helpdesk staff, technical support staff, application developers and SPAWAR SSC LANT customers.RSRS also includes Remedy on the SIPRNET for C4I trouble ticket tracking and SPAWAR CASREP Response Action Tracker (SCRAT) which is used for notification, dissemination, coordination, aggregation and tracking of technical assistance by In-Service Engineering Agents designated by SPAWAR 4.0 in-service support policy.  It provides the quantitative information to perform analytical assessment of processes and C4I system sustainment.  SCRAT provides SPAWARSYSCOM visibility into the effectiveness of In-service support technical assistance processes and policies.  Data accumulated gives the SPAWAR enterprise the ability to quickly assign, track, task, resolve and assess C4I system degradations impacting fleet readiness.  Supports tactical, operational and strategic command level visibility for SPAWAR and SPAWAR supported C4I systems readiness degradations.

ESGR promotes the importance of employer support through regular communications to military leadership, and serves as a communication link between employers and the Department of Defense.  ESGR's Portal has three parts:  ? ESGR Public web site (www.esgr.mil) ? This site informs and educates service members and their civilian employers regarding their rights and responsibilities under the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act (USERRA) law and to request assistance in resolving related disputes; provide a means for service members to recognize supportive employers through ESGR?s awards program; and for employers to request a Statement of Support to show their support for their service members.  ESGR serves as a free resource to 11 million employers and 800,000 service members.  The site includes a webpage for each of the 54 State ESGR Committees.  ? ESGR Freedom Award Web site (www.freedomaward.mil) ? ESGR and Department of Defense (DoD) honors employers providing exceptional support with the Secretary of Defense Employer Support Freedom Award.  This site is a means to advertise this award and the path for nominations.  ? ESGR Portal - The system is a secure application with role-based access for ESGR staff and volunteers.  The system includes three modules: the Inquiry and Case Management System (ICMS), Member Management System (MMS), and Freedom Award Nomination (FAN).  ICMS allows ESGR to enter, track and resolve inquiries and mediation cases associated with the USERRA support ; MMS allows ESGR to track ESGR membership, membership training, and hours volunteers worked for over 4,900 volunteers in 54 State Committees (MMS), plus HQ ESGR staff; and FAN allows ESGR to process Freedom Award Nominations.

investmentDescription: The Automated Case Tracking System (ACTS) is the AF Inspector General (IG) single case management system used by every level of IG to record all IG investigative and administrative activity AF-wide. ACTS allows for electronic transfer of IG records from IG offices throughout the world through the Major Commands (MAJCOMs) to the Headquarters AF (HAF). This process removes the need to mail hard copy case files, speeding up the statutorily-required case review process, and allows for a completely paperless case file. ACTS allows for continuous oversight of IG complaints resolution records, from cradle to grave. ACTS allows for continuous and instantaneous updating of case files. Centralized storage of electronic records allows for efficient backup and archiving of records. A major concern of Congress was the length of time it takes for cases brought under 10 USC 1034, Military Whistleblower Protection Act. ACTS allows for access to cases 24/7 worldwide. This significantly enhances and speeds the oversight of cases that need review according to 10 USC 1034 and AFI 90-301, Inspector General Complaints Resolution Program. All persons who make complaints to the AF IG are the primary beneficiaries of the investment. This includes all military members, DoD civilians, dependents and civilians unaffiliated with the AF. ACTS has no dependencies on other investments.  The organizations that currently use this capability are: the Air Force Inspector General (IG), Africa Command IG, Central Command IG, Defense Contracting Audit Agency IG, European Command IG, Northern Command IG, Secretary of the Air Force Legislative Liaison (SAF/LLM), Southern Command IG, US Forces Korea IG, and US Transportation Command IG. The Air Force, as well as the other Defense Agencies using ACTS, benefit from the quick and reliable access to complainant cases, easing resolution of complaints.  ACTS relies on a ColdFusion server and an Oracle Server. The Secretary of the Air Force Complaints Resolution Directorate (SAF/IGQ), the Secretary of the Air Force Administrative Assistant Enterprise Business Solutions (SAF/AAIE), and the 844th Communications Group (844 CG) manage various aspects of ACTS.  There are no earlier incarnations of ACTS.

investmentDescription: AFIPPS will be a web enabled, Commercial-Off-The-Shelf (COTS)-based solution aligning with the Secretary of the Air Force (SECAF) "3 to 1" (Regular Air Force [RegAF], Air National Guard [ANG], and Air Force Reserve [AFRes]) initiative dated October 15, 2010 that will integrate many existing personnel and pay processes into one self-service system. The system represents the AF commitment to modernizing business practices and providing enhanced support for today's service members and their families. AFIPPS will align with DoD data standards for personnel, pay, and accounting, including the Common Human Resource Information Standards (CHRIS), which will ensure compliance with the Business Enterprise Architecture (BEA). AFIPPS will provide Enterprise Information Web (EIW) services. The AFIPPS program will be bound by using the BEA "Hire-to-Retire" (H2R) construct. AFIPPS is designed to successfully modernize 84% of the AF'S BEA H2R level-one activities.  The purpose of AFIPPS is to provide the AF with a sustainable, cost-effective, auditable and regulatory compliant method of effectively capturing and maintaining personnel information so that Service members are paid accurately and on-time without requiring repetitive action or onerous paperwork, while allowing commanders/managers to easily access pertinent information.  The goal of AFIPPS is to fully integrate personnel and pay management for the AF's Total Force (RegAF, ANG, and AFRes). The future state will be characterized by streamlined, Total Force business processes; efficient and accurate management of pay entitlements; auditable financial statements with regard to military pay; improved access to accurate and timely personnel data for authorized users; and a modernized IT systems environment that is cost-effective and can adapt to future needs.  AFIPPS's customers include approximately 507,000 AF Service members across all components (330,000 RegAF, 107,000 ANG, and 70,000 AFRes) as well as thousands of military leaders of different ranks, specialties, and career fields who are responsible for the conduct of AF operations that rely on these services to ensure Service members with the appropriate skill sets are deployed where needed at home and on the battlefield. Congress, the rest of the Department of Defense (DoD), and other federal agencies all rely on accurate AF Human Resources (HR) data to make key decisions that affect how the US military is organized, funded, deployed, and maintained.

investmentDescription:
The NCIC is an FBI information system that contains records contributed by federal, state, local, tribal, and territorial criminal justice agencies.  Records are organized into different types of Person and Property Files within NCIC.  These records are then accessible to criminal justice agencies and authorized non-criminal justice agencies nationwide 24 hours a day, 365 days a year.  The system contains over 19 million active records in 22 different files, processes millions of transactions per day, and delivers critical results in microseconds. The NCIC System has been called the lifeline of law enforcement.

The information contained in the NCIC System assists FBI partners with numerous criminal justice duties, such as apprehending wanted persons, locating missing persons, identifying stolen property, and providing criminal justice information pertaining to gangs, domestic and foreign terrorists, and those individuals who pose a physical threat to the public or law enforcement.

The NCIC System serves criminal justice agencies in the fifty states, the District of Columbia, U.S. Territories, and Canada, as well as federal criminal justice agencies.  The NCIC System is available to criminal justice agencies through established law enforcement systems.  Additionally, specific foreign agencies have access to NCIC data provided through INTERPOL United States National Central Bureau.

The FBI is charged by Title 28, Code of Federal Regulations, Section 20, as manager of the system.  Currently inclusive in the system is the host computer and associated equipment located at the Criminal Justice Information Services Division's main facility in Clarksburg, WV, and the disaster recovery system located at Pocatello, ID.

By August 2026, the NCIC System is projected to transition from mainframes to an AWS cloud platform.  The migration of the NCIC to the cloud includes an extensive modernization of system architecture to optimize the delivery of features and functionality to NCIC law enforcement partners and other stakeholders.

The RIS system supports maximum cross flow of information during mission execution via distributed access to required SOF headquarters radio nets (Command, Fires, Air, Maritime, Coalition, Combat Search and Rescue, etc.). investmentDescription: The Assured Neuro Symbolic Learning and Reasoning (ANSR) program, building on results derived in the Engineering Artificial Intelligence Systems Implementations (EAISI) program (PE 0602303E, Project IT-04), will develop new hybrid AI algorithms that deeply integrate symbolic reasoning with data driven learning to create trustworthy AI-based systems. Here, an AI based system is considered trustworthy if it is: (a) robust to domain informed and adversarial perturbations, (b) supported by an assurance framework that creates and analyzes heterogenous evidence towards safety and risk assessments, and (c) predictable with respect to some specification and model of fitness. ANSR will develop hybrid AI algorithms for which it is possible to develop evidence based techniques that support confident assurance judgments. The key idea is to interleave symbolic and neural representations in hybrid AI algorithms that are capable of acquiring symbolic knowledge through learning and performing symbolic reasoning at scale to deliver robust inference, generalize to new situations, and provide evidence for assurance and trust. The ANSR concept and framework are agnostic to the specific neural methods (deep learning, reinforcement learning, etc.) used, and therefore will be broadly applicable. ANSR technologies will be demonstrated and evaluated on DoD use cases such as autonomy where trustworthiness is essential.

investmentTitle: DFAS INTERNAL REVIEW CASE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM
investmentDescription: The DFAS Internal Review Criminal Investigation Branch (DICIB) investigates violations of US law, DoD, DFAS, or Military Service instructions, regulations and policies. Investigations result from hotline, audits, anonymous tips, proactive initiatives, or by management requests. The Areas of investigations include:  Inappropriate Use of Government Equipment, Travel Fraud, Time & Attendance, Worker's Compensation, and Retired and Annuity Death Pay.  The current method performing case management does not achieve 100% compliance with Council of the Inspectors General on Integrity and Efficiency (CIGIE) standards and does not obtain parity with our investigation's counterparts for joint investigations.  A proven Investigations/Law Enforcement Case Management System solution will allow the DCIB to meet its goals to: Achieve 100% compliance with CIGIE standards and to obtain parity with our investigation's counterparts. Improve the quality of our investigations by having the ability to document case related information.   Improve transparency of investigations by putting all case related information into one system used for supervisory review. Increase efficiency as the solution will act as a repository for all case related documentation ensuring that these documents allow access for future inquiries. Identify repeat offenders and conduct analysis that will allow us to find links between cases and individuals (such as with diversion investigations involving multiple bank accounts, IP addresses, and other data points). Reduce the number of man hours required to track and generate statistics for reports on the activities of the Investigations Team to DFAS Management. Decrease the number of man hours required to generate and format investigative reports for DFAS Management, prosecutors, and outside law enforcement agencies working with us on joint investigations.  This will increase the efficiency of the reporting process for both Investigators and Supervisors as they conduct reviews and provide approval at the completion of each investigative activity, dramatically shortening the time between the last investigative steps and distributing the report to the decision-makers. This solution will provide a cost effective and reliable investigation DFAS case management system that provides functionality supporting modern case management processes, leverages advanced technology, and is flexible to legislative, mission or process changes.

A dedicated training and references repository within IGCAM provides an information sharing platform whereby users may share subject matter guidance, policy information, and download or upload files across the Command Inspector General (CIG) network. System logs are used to understand changes made to a case: when a case is created (dates/timestamps), changes within a case, or which users made the change. These logs may be used to support audit trails. IGCAM provides automated e-mail notifications and correspondence generation for users and complainants when a case is opened or closed. Complainants are notified of appropriate case information, assigned case personnel, and provided contact information.

investmentDescription: The Online Harvest Diary Surveys, when fully operational, will replace the former paper harvest survey that has been conducted by the USFWS Migratory Bird Program since the mid-1950s.  The Online Harvest Diary Surveys collects information on hunting activity and harvest of 5 groups of migratory birds:  waterfowl, doves and pigeons, woodcock, snipe/coot/rails/gallinules, and sandhill cranes.  The survey is sent to a sample of hunters who registered with the Harvest Information Program in the state in which they intend to hunt. investmentDescription: The Transfer from Imprecise and Abstract Models to Autonomous Technologies (TIAMAT) program will develop techniques to robustly transfer learned autonomy from fast abstract simulations to autonomous platforms in real-world environments. The autonomy levels of unmanned systems of today are limited because the modeling and simulation (M&S) training environments do not account for the data domain shift common when translating M&S outcomes to the real world - this phenomenon is sometimes referred to as the sim2real gap. The TIAMAT approach will integrate symbolic structures with neural structures to more realistically and robustly transfer learned autonomy.

investmentDescription: The Civil Law Case Management System (CLCMS) is a web-based legal case management system that assists Air Force legal professionals manage their legal cases and clients and keep cases associated with civil liability claims both on behalf and against the government.  CLCMS automates the daily workflow and complexities of civil litigation, improves managing case details, tracks and reports on case status, automates forms generation, suspense dates, and provides web-based queries and standard reports.  The application supports approximately 500 AF legal professionals globally with processing these cases.  There are four major functions provided by the application.  The Personal Property Claims (PPC) module allows thousands of airmen and veterans to initiate claims against the Air Force online for damage to their personal property.  These claims are normally associated with the movement of airmen and their families between bases but can also stem from natural disasters which occur at a military facility.  The system guides both the claimant and the claims examiner through a standard process to determine whether the compensation claimed is justified.  The system records the amount agreed upon and method of distribution to the recipient.  The Medical Claim Recovery Program (MCRP) module of the application supports paralegals and attorneys who investigate injuries sustain by military personnel which may be attributable to the negligence of third parties.  The application provides the legal professional with the documents necessary to initiate an investigation and tracks the overall progress of a claim through civil litigation (court) if necessary.  The general Torts module is utilized by Air Force attorneys across the globe to record a summary of the proceedings associated with a wide array of civil law based claims.  The International Agreement Claims Act (IACA) module allows JAG personnel overseas to summarize the disposition of claims made by foreign nationals.  The records within this system are used for claim/case evaluation, processing, and the management of claims/cases.  Records are also used as necessary in civil litigation involving the United States.  The system is supported by the Air Force Legal Information Services Directorate (AF/JAS) located at Maxwell AFB.

investmentDescription: On 12/12/2017 (approx.) the investment GIS Anniston's name was changed to ANAD GIS Anniston. Benefits are decision support for infrastructure decisions and management, crisis management, routine infrastructure maintenance, situational awareness, a common installation picture (CIP), serves as a central repository of installation infrastructure information, facilitates improvements and tracks investments, increases the timeliness of data and lowers information costs, allows for automated interaction on key engineering processes, provides centralized drawing records management, and map themes modules for quick access to layer groupings of the installation. It is currently utilized by directorates at ANAD: Directorate of Public Works (DPW), Directorate of Information Management (DOIM), Directorate of Risk Management (DRK), Directorate of Engineering and Quality (DEQ), and Directorate of Emergency Services (DES).  It has functional applications in 12 areas including facility management, air compliance, and dig permits.  It contains and allows real time access to over 70 data layers of maps such as utilities, buildings, roads, and fuel tanks; related systems such as FEMS, IFS, and HMMS, and over 25,000 documents including CAD, photos, procedures, and equipment manuals.  Users use menus and a Google-like/ search utility to navigate and query the system.  It saves time by allowing users to access their information in one location rather than the four separate systems and lowers information maintenance costs by enabling information to be managed by custodians depot-wide.  Removal of this system would lose the time and data maintenance cost savings this system provides and lose the synergy gained by having all the depots infrastructure information in one location.

The 2015 NDAA also:   -directs communication with families, concerned citizens, and veteran service organizations about efforts to account for missing personnel;   -allows the new defense agency to enter into public/private partnerships to account for missing personnel;   -allows the agency to enter into cooperative agreements and accept gifts to support accounting;   -appoints a Medical Examiner to oversee Identifications and Laboratory Operations of the agency;  -and directs the agency to establish and maintain a single centralized database and case management system on all missing persons.  In August 2013, the OSD Designated Approval Authority (DAA) requested that the former Defense Prisoner of War/Missing Personnel Office (DPMO) transition its IT network infrastructure off of the OSD network in preparation for this new agency.  DPAA has just completed its network merger on to the former Joint POW/Accounting Community?s (JPAC) Non-classified Internet Protocol Router (NIPR) and will soon merge on to the former JPAC?s Secret Internet Protocol Router (SIPR) network.  The accounting community?s untold sacrifices and numerous achievements have justly brought final resolution to the families of many of our lost service members and DoD civilians.  This mission requires strong information management support, from collecting and analyzing information to producing and managing documents in a wide variety of paper and electronic formats.  As the personnel accounting community continues merging, we carry on collaboration, consolidation and operations both CONUS and OCONUS.  Moreover, we maintain communications with the larger community of interest by expanding public/private partnerships in order to enhance mission capability.  In support of the mission, we are enhancing personnel, hardware and software support of the new agency.  This includes upgrading services and leveraging industry best practices on the merged NIPR, SIPR and the Joint Worldwide Intelligence Communications System (JWICS) networks.

partOfITPortfolio: Part 2. IT Investments for Mission Support Services
investmentTitle: Process Order Development and Display System
investmentDescription: The Process Order Development and Display System (PODDS) is a system that facilitates the electronic implementation of AFMC Form 561 as defined by AFI21-101, subsection 19.3, Preparing Process Orders.  PODDS facilitates the creation, maintenance, coordination and distribution of electronic process orders which contain specific overhaul and repair process information for various USAF aircraft parts. Process engineers use PODDS to prepare, modify and control all process orders in the system.  Engineers write procedures for overhaul processes and attach electronic pictures, diagrams, video, tables or other forms of media that help explain correct processing methods.  As process orders are modified, PODDS stores previous versions in an archive as part of audit trail requirements. Coordination and authorization of process orders takes place automatically in PODDS, requiring appropriate review and approval from Safety, Quality, Planning and Production personnel.  The system sends email notifications throughout the process to streamline approval.  Once a process order is approved, it is published for ready-only access over the web.  The system also allows for the creation of PDF versions of process orders.  Maintenance personnel and especially shop floor mechanics use the process orders over the web as they follow critical overhaul procedures. The system automatically monitors process orders, enforcing required reviews at predefined intervals as well as deactivating process orders that expire before appropriate reviews have taken place.  PODDS also provides reporting mechanisms for engineers and managers to inspect the current status of process orders, their level of activity as well as the current process order reviews in the system. This is a "Server" based application This investment is covered under the Hill Enterprise Data Center (HEDC), hosting system EITDR# BI0009HS

investmentDescription: The Pharmacy Outpatient Automation Solution ? ScriptPro provides pharmacy workflow management and automated medication fulfillment technologies.  Activities associated with the storage, dispensing and distribution of medications are supported through the capabilities to track movement accurately throughout the dispensing process.  The POAS-S maintains detailed transaction information, which enables increased security, accuracy, and accountability of medications.  Patient safety enhancements that reduce the risk of medication errors are realized through the utilization of embedded checks and balances employed within the pharmacy workflow management software.  Standardized workflows increase productivity and efficiencies associated with the medication dispensing process, which facilitates a culture focused on direct patient care.  In addition, the POAS-S integrates telepharmacy videoconferencing technology with pharmacy operations management software.  System elements can be located at both central pharmacy and remote telepharmacy sites permitting pharmacists at central pharmacies access a patient?s medication profile and perform a prospective drug utilization review by computer on each prescription before dispensing to the patient at a remote site.  Through use of telepharmacy technology, remote pharmacy services provide the same quality standards used in traditional pharmacy practice including pharmacist prescription verification before dispensing, drug utilization review, and patient education counseling.  Pharmacists using telecommunications technology can systematically provide personalized electronically documented, real-time professional services to patients at a remote location, including prescription dispensing and counseling, and supervise remote pharmacy operations.

investmentDescription: This system is similar to any college electronic student record system except we have a lot more information to gather. Since the legacy Honeywell system, Defense English Language Management Information System (DELMIS), was discontinued we needed to have a system to replace it and we developed the SDMS system. DELMIS's authority to maintain was 10 U.S.C. 8013, Secretary of the Air Force: powers and duties; delegation by; as implemented by Air Force Instruction 16-103/OPNAVINST 1550.11/MCO 1550.24, Management of the Defense English Language Program; and E.O. 9397 (SSN). We imported the information from the legacy DELMIS system and have added more capability. Most of our students change class every week and they are tested each week. Therefore we track each class and the test results. We have several types of test. We use computer delivered testing (CDT), Proficiency Exams (PE), English Comprehension Level (ECL) and oral proficiency interview (OPI) tests. CDTs are given weekly on the class attended. ECLs are given weekly to incoming students and monthly to all the students. OPIs are administered as required. Students must reach a prescribed ECL score before they are allowed to attend their follow on training. Depending on the follow on training, i.e. pilot training; the student must also attain a prescribed OPI score. All of the test scores are maintained in the database. We track attendance and access points for absences and tardy's. We track medical appointments, physical training attendance and flight physicals. We also maintain teacher and supervisor comments on students progress. The database also maintains all personal information pertinent to a foreign student.

FPDS-NG - Federal Procurement Data System-Next Generation is one of those 9 systems.  According to section 4.602(a) of the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR), FPDS-NG provides a comprehensive mechanism for assembling, organizing, and presenting contract placement data for the Federal Government. Agencies must report all transactions over the micropurchase threshold (currently $3,500) and modifications to those transactions regardless of dollar value (including no-cost modifications). investmentDescription:
The RIA-JMTC Distributed Numeric Controls (DNC) system provides electronic distribution of part program files from a central server to a distributed network of workstations.  The workstations in turn communicate with up to 400 Computer Numerical Control (CNC) machines and tools via direct serial interface.  Work is under way to fully integrate the CNC machines across the network, eliminating the serial connection.  The DNC system utilizes Predator COTS software for managing system security.  Each system feature/function/role is assignable by authenticated user ID.  The DNC system also provides a controlled environment for Machinists to edit part program data while performing program prove-outs and prototype work.  The system captures and logs any changes to manufacturing part program data insuring the integrity of the manufacturing process. The DNC system is utilized in the manufacture of all parts and end items produced by RIA-JMTC and supports approximately 300 artisans and users.

In FY11, RIA-JMTC completed a pilot project to enhance our DNC system with the capabilities of the Predator Manufacturing Data Collection (MDC) tool as part of the system on a select number of CNC machines.  MDC is utilized to collect (push from the machine & pull remotely) machine performance and utilization data to assist in capacity planning as well as predictive and preventative machine maintenance data.  Work is underway to quantify a Capital Investment Project for FY14 that will add the MDC client capability on all CNC machines in the factory.  Benefits include the capability to manage up to 400 Computer Numerically Controlled machines from a networked computer to cut steel and produce parts.  The system is a large time saver as it is used for the electronic transfer of CNC CAD/CAM designed parts for weapon systems.

investmentDescription: The Wholesale Inventory Optimization Model for Enterprise Resource Planning (WIOM-ERP) consists of three main components, (1) WIOM5Reader, (2) a discrete event simulation (DRPSim), and (3) an optimization model (WIOM-OPT).  The toolset is modular, allowing the user flexibility in how to employ it.    WIOM5Reader contains the graphical user interface (GUI) as well as all required functions required to interface with NAVSUP?s NDP environment.  Raw transactional data, to include historical requisitions, repairs, and procurements are combined with item attribute information (prices, current forecast values, weapon system) and state variables (current inventory posture, due-ins) to create a WIOM input set.  Input sets can contain millions of rows of transactional data.  WIOM5Reader automatically handles data extraction from NDP, as well as conducting required validation and restructuring.  DRPSim is a discrete event simulation that models the supply system against multiple stochastically generated synthetic futures.   The simulation models both internal events, like Distributed Requirements Planning (DRP) calculations, as well as external events, such as commercial repair initiations, customer demands, and retrograde returns.  WIOM-OPT is a multi-objective optimization model that seeks Planned Minimum Safety Stock Level (PMSSL) values that are globally optimal for all items simultaneously considered.  Objective values can be specified as either achievements (maximize or minimize a metric), or as deviations (minimize the difference between a metric value and a goal) from targets.  WIOM-OPT establishes weights at the item or metric level with the optimization model framework designed to give large amounts of flexibility to the user.

investmentTitle: Planning Resource for Infrastructure Development and Evaluation
investmentDescription: The comprehensive enterprise system of the Army National Guard Installation and Environment Directorate (ARNG-I&E) replaces legacy IT systems and processes to meet unique requirements emerging from both State and Federal entities across all 54 States and Territories. The commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) product, IBM TRIRIGA, while used by many state and federal agencies, provides agile solutions to meet unique ARNG facility management, planning, and programming requirements. The system covers a variety of enterprise-level processes at both State and Federal levels which include: real property accountability, military construction prioritization and execution, capital improvements, sustainment projects, facility maintenance, facility base operations requirements approval, facility planning, space management, facility related controls systems (FRCS) inventory and tracking, energy management, grid security, utility billing, industrial hygiene tracking, environmental management, and sustainability. This Integrated Workplace Management System (IWMS) provides agile tools with built-in ability to customize workflows and data fields to simultaneously meet ARNG State and Federal missions when other federal Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems are not scoped to meet governing State requirements. By design, while common processes do exist across all 54 States, the system provides the means to adapt data fields, reports, classifications, and specifications when one or more States have varying or unique requirements. States manage these variations, generate custom reporting, and perform process adaptations at their level. This critical architecture functionality provides solutions that avoid 54 separate software packages while retaining enterprise level resourcing. Its highly configurable interface provides role-based functions and automates processes and approvals for configured services without directly modifying the COTS software platform. ARNG performs workflow modifications and business process adaptations with teams and change control boards (CCBs) comprised of members directly responsible for meeting requirements and master planning as they interface directly with States and various agencies. System users include the I&E Directorate personnel, Construction and Facility Management Offices (CFMO), Department of Public Works (DPW), G6, G8, and any State and Federal ARNG employee (including Soldiers) that requests facility services.

Eagle eTIMS is used by the USAF F-15, F-22, and F-16 weapon systems. DLA and authorized prime contractors also use the system to generate large parts and tooling savings for DOD. The system provides program and logistics manager's unique instantaneous aircraft special tooling (ST) availability and applicability data required for a wide variety of acquisition and sustainment situations. eTIMS provides instant tooling (ST) logistics support analysis (LSA). Its speed allows managers to make rapid, cost effective, acquisition decisions, providing available tooling to expedite the procurement and repair of spare parts to meet fleet requirements. eTIMS also provides a complete aircraft parts breakdown, as the aircraft is manufactured, along with the tooling required to manufacture each part. It identifies tooling required and tooling inventory available to produce the needed parts. Additionally, eTIMS provides a complete inventory of tools and masters available including status and location. eTIMS is very successful in reducing the cost of production line shutdowns. Production tooling disposition analysis is based on a weapon system specific supportability algorithm that incorporates past and projected requirements and the tooling on hand. Through its use, critical tooling is maintained; production line shutdown costs reduced and the delivery of parts for spares and modifications programs are expedited. Increased visibility of tooling availability and applicability has generated many millions of dollars in savings through special tools reproduction cost avoidance. ROI exceeds 22 to 1.

investmentTitle: MEDICAL COMMUNICATIONS FOR COMBAT CASUALTY CARE
investmentDescription: MC4 provides the Army's solution to Presidential and Congressional objectives, set-forth by Title 10 in 1997, which called for a medical tracking system for all deployed Service members.  MC4 integrates Defense Health   Systems' (DHS) Theater Medical Information Program-Joint (TMIP-J) software, and other Army-unique applications, onto commercial and government-off-the-shelf technology, providing the tools needed to digitally record and transfer critical medical data from the foxhole to medical treatment facilities worldwide. MC4 is a ruggedized system containing joint software applications fielded to tactical medical forces throughout the combat zone, the U.S., and contingency operations worldwide.  Deployable medical forces use the MC4 system to gain quick, accurate access to patient histories and forward casualty resuscitation information. The system also provides units with automated tools facilitating patient tracking, medical reporting, and medical logistical support. Combatant commanders use the MC4 system to access medical surveillance information, resulting in enhanced medical situational awareness. Most importantly, MC4 is helping deployed Service members. By equipping deployed medical units with automated resources, MC4 helps ensure Service members have a secure, accessible, lifelong electronic medical record, which results in better-informed health care providers and easier access to Veterans Administration medical benefits. The MC4 system comprises seven Army-approved line items that can be configured to support Army levels 1-4 and DOD roles 1-3 of the health care continuum. Future MC4 enhancements will be accomplished through minor system upgrades and major planned upgrades. The MC4 program completed a successful full-rate production decision review on July 21, 2005. With over 15 years of experience managing the DOD's first battlefield medical recording system, MC4 remains the most widely-used, comprehensive information management medical system on the battlefield.

F-16 maintainers are tasked by F-16 SPO Engineering through varying means to inspect for structural cracks, corrosion issues, and to maintain various system and subsystem time sensitive inspection requirements. Inspection results are then analyzed to determine future maintenance and engineering actions necessary for managing F-16 fleet. Health of the Fleet (HOTF) and Service Life Reports (SLR) are used to provide Equivalent Flight Hours (EFH) for F-16 fleet lifecycle management. Current EFH versus certified service life analysis of each aircraft in F-16 fleet is critical to examine overall fleet and individual aircraft longevity for force structure and management purposes. This analysis enables F-16 ASIP to calculate structural health, maintenance and inspection requirements of individual F-16 aircraft/fleet, and to achieve superior structural safety performance levels. Flight Data Capture (FDC) application is how critical flight data recorder files are uploaded and managed. These files are used to understand how each individual aircraft flies in comparison to design/test baselines, which then in turn drives inspections and other maintenance requirements throughout life of the aircraft. Damage Evaluation System (DES) is used in the field to generate an incident report (AFTO Form 92) on site so quick decisions can be made as about the management of the aircraft involved. Structural Evaluation System (SES) contains Margin-of-Safety calculations and tools providing engineers with a consistent method for determining structural viability based on original F-16 stress specifications.

investmentDescription: The Aerospace Systems Directorate brings together world-class facilities including a fuels research facility, structural testing labs, compressor research facility, supersonic and subsonic wind tunnels, flight simulation lab, and many other cutting-edge research labs. Among the technologies in development in the Aerospace Systems Directorate are scramjet engines, alternative fuels, unmanned vehicles, hypersonic vehicles, collision avoidance and aircraft energy optimization. The Aerospace Systems Directorate at Wright-Patterson AFB uses these facilities to conduct its Research & Development mission and no general purpose processing is conducted in these facilities.  This SPPN supports special purpose functions that cannot be supported by CDCs, CEDCs, IPNs or Cloud due to its association with non-severable infrastructure or equipment tethered to non-IT hardware to carry out its R&D mission.  These facilities contain standalone networks/servers used by researchers to conduct tests and were combined for FDCCI into one SPPN (17462) that aren?t connected to AFNET. This SPPN requires physical isolation as testing and experimentation must be accomplished in controlled environments with no possible interruption.  In cases such as high speed wind tunnel experiments, interruption could cause damage to multi-million dollar test articles and test environments, and could cause safety issues in some cases during jet engine testing.  The test environments must also be isolated from AFNET since much of the hardware and software is unique and cannot be approved to run on AFNET.  As a result, the isolated servers and associated items are set up in close proximity with the test equipment and cannot be relocated to the base IPN or cloud. Additionally, the magnitude of data that is processed cannot be transmitted over the base network but traverses the Defense Research and Engineering Network.

partOfITPortfolio: Part 3. IT Standard IT Investments
investmentDescription: This is a Special Purpose Processing Node (SPPN) that supports AFRL Headquarters to conduct collaborative research, development, configuration, testing, and evaluations of products to support the implementation throughout the Air Force scientific research organizations.  New technologies and Information System Cybersecurity products are tested for network performance, functional capability, operational stability, and overall net worthiness.  These products could be software based, hardware based, or specialized purpose built appliances.  In order to make these determinations on untested products and capabilities, isolated networks utilizing high bandwidth uplinks are required in order to not interrupt other operational networks, while at the same time giving access to AFRL Headquarters researchers and engineers to evaluate the solutions.  The results of this testing provides warfighting capabilities to the Air Force space and cyberspace forces to ensure networks are being monitored, operated optimally, and defended against.   This SPPN also has a fully virtualized environment with components that require low latency such as Virtual Desktop Infrastructure (VDI).  Highly functioning and responsive VDI capabilities require sustained high bandwidth uplinks (2mbps ? 32mbps/client) for smooth graphical displays and input from the mouse and keyboard.  The proximity of the client to the VDI server directly reflects the latency and responsiveness of the client.  By placing the infrastructure in the SPPN, this reduces the number of network hops, therefore ensuring low latency and fewer connectivity failures.  Low latency in the VDI solution allows for a fully functional desktop to be used by a researcher or engineer without the risk for motion sickness due to irregular framerates and screen tearing.  The two examples provided could not be effectively deployed without interruption to other network services if the isolation and locality of the SPPN was not available to the AFRL Headquarters scientists and engineers. This SPPN does not conduct business or general purpose processing.  It is specifically established to support the research environment.

investmentDescription: The SeaPort Portal, whose core is a modified Commercial-Off-The-Shelf (COTS) system, provides a secure, automated procurement process, in which complex, professional support service requirements (with a value greater than $2,500) can be planned and tracked, developed, solicited, source selected, awarded, and administered using the Naval Sea Systems Command?s Multiple Award Contract (MAC) vehicle ?SeaPort.?   This vehicle, which is available for use only by Navy Contracting Officers, is comprised of an established and controlled contractor community, each qualified and capable to compete for various professional, engineering, and technical support services.  Based upon individual Program?s unique requirements, solicitations are developed for each acquisition and a subset of the contractor community are provided an opportunity to offer customized proposals.  Since the Portal is web-based, users around the globe are able to electronically receive, evaluate, and select winning proposals, using best value source selection methods, on-line and concurrently.  Vendors use the Portal to upload proposals, Small Business Subcontracting Plan information, and other proposal requirements (excluding Representations and Certifications). Once selected, task orders are prepared and awarded using legally binding digital signatures.  Task orders and modifications are generated by re-using the data captured during the requirements determination, proposal, and source selection processes, improving both the processing time and accuracy of contractual documents. Financial and Line item account information is exchanged with Navy financial systems. Additionally, solicitations, task orders and other contract documents are captured in an electronic resource library to provide models for future procurements. The e-procurement portal captures data on each step of the process to provide up-to-the-minute metrics and information required for Official Governmental reporting systems, such as PPIRS, EDA and FPDS-NG. The Portal also maintains the official contract file. This record also includes the Public Facing web-portal (eMASS ID 7782).

investmentDescription: The Joint Deficiency Reporting System is the single authoritative source for the Joint aviation warfighter to report deficiencies, notify stakeholders, guide support team investigation and response, compile investigation data, report problem resolution and prevent recurrence.  JDRS is a web-based application hosted and maintained by NAVAIRSYSCOM and provides complete visibility and interoperability of the deficiency reporting and investigative process in one application, allowing a seamless, standard deficiency reporting workflow process across the US Armed Forces: Navy, Marine Corp, Air Force, and Coast Guard (via MOA) and supporting agencies (DCMA, DLA, NASA, DCIS, NCIS).   The JDRS application connects the warfighter with their respective program, engineering, quality and logistics support teams in the standardized submission, investigation and resolution of deficiency reports that include:  Engineering Investigations and Hazardous Material Reports (EI/HMRs), Product Quality Deficiency Reports (PQDRs), Acceptance Inspection Deficiency Reports (AIDRs), Technical Publication Deficiency Reports (TPDRs), Information System Deficiency Reports (ISDRs), Aircraft Baseline Trouble Reports/Change Requests (BTR/BCRs), Aircraft Engine Foreign Object Damage Incident Reports (FOD-IR), Fleet Aircraft Material Condition Inspections (MCI), Depot Planner & Estimator (P&E) Requests for Fleet in-service repairs (ISRs), Depot Aircraft Delivery Deficiency Reports (ADDRs) and Retail DLA Technical Information Requests (RDR).  JDRS allows identification and notification of suspect counterfeit components and also includes a critical item management module, allowing identification and evaluation of aviation Critical Safety Items (CSIs). investmentDescription:
The purpose of the Base Information Transport Infrastructure (BITI) Wired (formerly known as Information Transport System (ITS) Increment (Inc) 1) is to install Active Duty, Reserve, and Air National Guard (ANG) base network backbone infrastructure required to meet increasing demand for high-speed network access. The goals of BITI Wired are to design, install and sustain high-speed network backbones using industry standard design methodologies and installation principles, eliminating design flaws, such as single points of failure, which occur as a result of patch-work network design and implementation. The current and anticipated benefits include providing the data, video and imagery supporting Air Force operations and providing a standard infrastructure allowing the 24th Air Force Commander to centrally manage and defend the Air Force network.

In order to accomplish the overall Air Force mission, warfighters require reliable, high speed access to combat and mission support systems. BITI Wired provides this capability by ensuring base networks have minimum required network throughput, survivability through reduced single points of failure and use of industry standard engineering practices.

BITI Wired supports base infrastructure and requires that only Joint Interoperability Test Command (JITC) Unified Capabilities (UC) Approved Product List (APL) material be purchased for installation.

The investment fully aligns with Joint Information Environment (JIE) by providing standards compliant installation level network backbones on Air Force installations as required by the warfighters to accomplish their missions. JIE is not driving new or additional base network architectural requirements, but only requires a network infrastructure to support UC.

The primary customers, stakeholders, and beneficiaries of BITI Wired are Air Force Major Commands, Direct Reporting Units, and Field Operating Agencies, Air Force Reserve and ANG, and Combatant Commands (Tenants) located on Air Force installations (United States Central Command (USCENTCOM), United States Transportation Command (USTRANSCOM), United States Northern Command (USNORTHCOM), United States Strategic Command (USSTRATCOM) and United States SpecialOperations Command (USSOCOM)) as well as the Defense Information Systems Agency.

The ESMS modules include BUILDER and ROOFER for assessing building conditions, PAVER for pavements, and RAILER for railroad infrastructure.  New modules being developed are Utilities SMS for utilities assets, and FUELER for fuel systems. Current requirements include data interface with the Installation Status Report (ISR) system to properly transfer data with additional Army systems. Additionally, ongoing work will be required to consolidate modules and modernize the Enterprise SMS software/suite. SMS provides the Army, the OSD required standardized process, for calculation of the Facility Condition Index (FCI), facility condition inventory, assessments, work requirements analysis, and forecasting. On 10 September 2013, the Under Secretary of Defense directed all the Services to adopt the Sustainment Management System (SMS) Suite consisting of the BUILDER, PAVER, and RAILER and other modules being developed to assess the condition of their real property facilities and to compute the Facility Condition Index (FCI).  Congress expressed concerns that the Services were not conducting facility condition assessments in a consistent manner, leading to inaccurate funding decisions.  The FCIs generated across the Services were not using the same evaluation tools and computational methods.  In the 2012 NDAA, Congress directed DoD to correct this problem.  To resolve this issue, the Army must integrate the FCI data generated in the SMS evaluations, with information in the Headquarters Installation Information System (HQIIS) and Installation Status Report (ISRWEB).

investmentTitle: Enterprise Land Mobile Radio C2 Network Services
investmentDescription: Current Base, Post, Station (BPS) Land Mobile Radio (LMR) architectures are fragmented.
