This increment of capability is called the "E-LMR (Slice)" in support of the Consolidated Emergency Response System was approved for Material Solution Analysis in a Commander MCSC MDD dated 18 Aug 2010. The Mapper system serves as the single, standard unclassified web portal for geospatial data covering all US Army training areas and ranges.  The Mapper website provides easy access for Commanders, G/S-3s, Master Gunners, trainers, training planners, schedulers, and other persons supporting or conducting US Army, joint, and multinational training.  Spatial datasets available for web based viewing and analysis include high resolution aerial / satellite imagery, topographic, elevation, and vector datasets, covering all Army training areas to include Forward Operating Sites.  Online functionality includes, but is not limited to, viewing, measuring, historical trend analysis, query builder, area search, plot layouts; with functionality upgrades including surface danger zone and  range footprint generation operational NLT end FY06.  

The Mapper system resources are organized under the US Army Sustainable Range Program OCONUS Regional Support Center, located in Grafenwoehr, Germany.  DA G3 (DAMO-TRS), Army Training Support Center, and 7th US Army Joint Multinational Training Command are the primary proponents of the Mapper system.  The Army Range Mapper is interlinked with multiple APMS systems, to include the Geographic Information System Repository (GISR) and Training Resource Management System (TRMS).  The Mapper has been running 24/7 since Feb 2003 and has serviced >10K unique customers totaling >4M hits.  The URL is https://srp.usareur.army.mil.

investmentDescription: The Open Price Exploration for National security (OPEN) program aims to increase supply chain resilience and enable more efficient critical mineral markets by leveraging advances in artificial intelligence (AI) prediction and forecasting to increase price, supply, and demand transparency. Based on concepts developed in the LogX Program (budgeted in PE 0603760E, Project CCC-02), OPEN will construct structural price predictions from fundamental and observable critical mineral input costs and increase the accuracy and precision of supply and demand forecasts by leveraging this structural price in conjunction with advances in AI and economic modeling. Today, critical mineral markets and supply chains are vulnerable. International supply shocks can lead to large and rapid critical mineral price spikes with immediate economic ramifications, and commodities purchase transactions (e.g., offtake agreements) are negotiated leveraging a mix of opaque and flawed pricing data. OPEN will leverage a decomposition of a critical mineral price into four components (input costs, supply/demand shocks, distortions due to noncompetitive behavior, and stochastic fluctuation) to construct transparent estimations of an approximate marginal cost for critical minerals indexed by time and geographic location, and will estimate supply and demand forecasts for critical minerals that take into account geopolitical factors, energy fluctuations, and technological  innovations in recycling and supply chain management. Technology developed under this program will transition to the Services and commercial partners.

The IDE will enable the Chief Engineer and ICBM  engineering workforce,  to ensure that all of these systems (Codes Systems, Ground Systems, Launch systems, Propulsion, Guidance, Reentry System/Reentry Vehicle, etc.) are available as they exercise Operational Safety, Suitability, and Effectiveness (OSS&E).  ICBM IDE enables the Chief Engineer to provide the OSS&E certification and authorization of the ICBM weapon. The IDE benefits the ICBMSD and the Air Force Nuclear Weapons Center (AFNWC) by providing a centralized location for all ICBM weapon system sustaining engineering analysis of the ICBM Weapon System (Minuteman III). The IDE will store unclassified weapon system analysis data, to include: test, cost, schedule, inventory, requirements, configuration, risk, and performance data used by engineers in the field for analyzing the weapon system. The analysis is to ensure current and future accuracy, maintainability, reliability, predictability, availability, supportability and sustainability critical to the ICBM and GBSD mission. The IDE integrates engineer analysis for users across multiple locations for Government and industry. The primary beneficiaries of this system will be ICBMSD, AFNWC, 20th Air Force (AF), and United States Strategic Command (USSTRATCOM) stakeholders and engineers including contractor personnel as assigned. Implementation of the ICBM IDE system resolves the challenge of shifting total system performance responsibilities for the ICBM from a contractor owned engineering analysis suite, back to a Government owned and managed sustaining engineering construct. Additionally, this system allows the ICBMSD to provide transition support of industrial ICBM technical expertise and knowledge to the ICBM organic workforce. The IDE is based on configurable Commercial Off The Shelf (COTS) software. The ICBM IDE is Government Owned, Contractor Operated (GOCO).

Continuous evaluation of the same key traits across all levels of the leadership continuum facilitates ongoing reinforcement of critical leadership traits through an operator?s career. It will also enhance identification of an individual?s tactical profile and assist in identifying training trends that indicate aptitude and interest in specific high-demand/low density qualifications.  CLD will develop better special operator teammates by continuously reinforcing and evaluating appropriate attributes, behaviors, and performance traits required for successful mission accomplishment. Routine anonymous feedback, blind-spot removal, engaged leadership, NSW ethos reinforcement, trend and artifact tracking, and aptitude assessment all contribute to creating and maintaining the consummate special operator.  The CLD program will be implemented throughout the NSW enterprise. The combination of continuous feedback and enhanced data analysis will directly enhance individual and unit effectiveness and lead to a more capable and adaptive fighting force.

This allows acquisition professionals and senior leaders to target improvement opportunities such as benefits gained via consolidated purchases allowing the AF to take advantage of quantity discounts. Prior to CBIS, acquisition people issued data requests to over 100 AF contracting offices and combined hundreds or even thousands of spreadsheets?a difficult and time consuming process?to conduct the type of analysis available now in the single location through CBIS. CBIS is documented as an initiative to comply with IT budget reporting for the functional support to the hosting GCSS-AF Data Services system.  AFMC aligns CBIS under its portfolio management process and AFMC/PK and AFMC/A4 personnel review CBIS capabilities semi-annually to ensure CBIS meets mission goals and objectives with the least possible lifecycle cost and program risk. investmentDescription: The Aviation and Missile Command Safety Interim Hazard Classification (AMCOM SIHC) provides a method of maintaining a complete and accurate database of AMCOM SIHC data, so an AMCOM SIHC memorandum and other reporting can be generated.  This program supports the larger Department of Defense/Department of Transportation (DoD/DOT) requirements to provide Interim Hazard Classifications (AMCOM SIHC) to our customers for their Ammunition and Explosives (AE) in need of transportation on public highways or being stored on DoD installations.  Under federal law and defined in DoD publications, all AE tested, used, produced, and transported by DoD agencies or their contracted support organizations must have AMCOM SIHCs on their articles throughout the items life cycle, or until a final hazard classification (FHC) can be received from DOT. This product is the repository for all data required to complete an AMCOM SIHC on an article. investmentDescription: AFAA MIS is a web-based application that functions as a central repository for unclassified AFAA internal audits. The AFAA MIS provides computer support to satisfy management requirements established by DoDIG, HQ USAF, AFAA headquarters, Directorates, and Regions. The main benefit is the system?s ability to maintain audit project and report information for current and five-prior fiscal years for mission reporting needs described above. The efficiencies of the system?s modular designs allows the agency to record data for management of current audit projects; account and summarize Centrally Directed Audits and local audit reports issued; input and summarize resource expenditure; and track annual continuing professional education requirements and deficiency. investmentDescription: The Automated Military Justice Analysis & Management System (AMJAMS) is a web-based system used to process and track the handling of disciplinary cases within the Air Force. The system provides case detail and statistical reports for all levels of command within the Air Force Judge Advocate General's Corps (AFJAGC) as well as in response to requests for disciplinary data from the Secretary of the Air Force, Secretary of Defense, Congress and the White House. The system and supporting functions address the processing, timeliness, standardization, and reporting on the adjudication of violations of the Uniform Code of Military Justice (UCMJ) and non-UCMJ disciplinary misconduct. Additionally, it includes the tracking of event calendaring and witness data. The system reduces processing errors by standardizing processes, producing the primary forms and enforcing data validation consistent with applicable Air Force Instructions and policies. Use of the system and supporting functions is mandatory within AFJAGC for the processing of UCMJ and non-UCMJ disciplinary cases. The system and supporting functions standardize the processing of disciplinary cases and provides access to reporting and query capabilities essential to monitoring the overall health of discipline at all levels. Additionally the standardized processing of cases reduces the time and resources necessary to train newly assigned personnel by eliminating locally established processes. AMJAMS imports, via a flat file, personnel data from the Military Personnel Data System (MILPDS) which is used to populate personnel data as cases are created. Without this import AMJAMS users would be required to manually enter in excess of 60 distinct data points for each new case. Legal offices at the base level, as well as NAF and MAJCOM legal offices, use AMJAMS and supporting functions. Currently, there are 194 different offices using the system and supporting functions; this includes active duty offices, Air National Guard offices, and Category A Reserve offices. The Air Force Legal Operations Directorate of Legal Information Services (AFLOA/JAS) manages day-to-day operations, maintaining the code and system and the Judge Advocate Functional Servers (JAFS) is the host for AMJAMS.

On 30 Oct 02, ASAFM&C finalized its decision to pursue the FC initiative, and on 13 Mar 03, the Secretary of the Army approved implementation of the FC program.  Through its stated objectives, FC has simplified the obligation process, alleviated cumbersome supply to finance reconciliation processes, and provided the Active Army, Army Reserves and Army National Guard with an automated process with which to control funds.  

There are four stated objectives of Funds Control and one substantial benefit derived.  Eliminate Installation Supply Buffer (ISB).  ISB is the current non-accounting DFAS, which operates between the SARSS / MW and ODS / STANFINS.  Obligate customer funds on the initial supply order/request. investmentDescription: The Training and Operational Readiness Information Services (TORIS) is a web-centric, enterprise-level, data collection, transfer, storage/warehousing, and decision support system designed to capture war fighter mission area training and sustainment proficiency information from the surface fleet. TORIS solves the critical issue of how to collect watch team training performance data without unnecessary burdening of our war-fighters aboard fleet units. Built and maintained by Afloat Training Group Pacific (ATGPAC) for use at the "deck plate" level, training assessors can capture data digitally during training scenarios conducted in operational environments under time-tested procedures and send this information to centralized servers for warehousing and further analysis. TORIS is the information system that underpins the Surfaces Force Readiness Manual (SFRM) and the Surface Force Exercise Manual (SFEM) and is the primary enabler for the Surface Warfare Enterprise (SWE) continuous readiness initiative. TORIS is the authoritative source for watch team training performance data from the surface fleet and is a critical data feed for all stakeholders of the unit level training (ULT) process. TORIS captures watch team training information generated during assessments conducted in operational environments aboard surface ships, data that supports those assessments (e.g. scheduling, trainer assignment, etc), and associated metrics on the operational readiness of Surface Force units. Outputs also include unit level training proficiency information for "Big Navy" dashboards and reporting systems such as NTIMS and DRRS-N.  The system does not contain or process classified information.
